engagement_title: Flagship shop launch for a Bristol steel frame builder: rescue the lost wordmark, unify a mixed light workshop shoot, rebuild the eight build spec book from last season's price list PDF, and produce the opening week window, poster, press page and social kit
vertical: Retail and consumer goods: independent bicycle manufacturer opening its first physical flagship store (Bristol, UK)
client_one_liner: We open our first shop in March and we need the whole launch kit built out of a shoot that does not match, a logo whose artwork no longer exists, and a spreadsheet three different people kept badly.
client_brief:
Thornbeck Cycles builds steel road and randonneur frames by hand in Bristol. Eleven years in a railway arch selling direct, and in March we open our first actual shop: a converted print works on Redcliffe Street, with the workshop visible from the pavement, eight complete builds on the floor and framesets to order. We need a launch kit for opening week, and it needs to hold together, because right now nothing we have does.

The photography. We shot the eight floor bikes, plus a close detail of the lugwork and a wide of the room, over two afternoons in the workshop. Half of it was daylight off the north window and half was under the overhead lamps after four o'clock, so the set is all over the place: some frames read blue and flat, some read orange, one is a stop darker than the rest, and one of them the tripod got knocked so the floor line runs downhill. Bring the whole shoot to one look, cool and clean and workshop honest, with the polish on the lugs and the chrome held rather than blown out. They have to sit next to each other in a catalogue without a customer noticing they were shot on different days. Before you build anything expensive off the back of the grade, put the whole set somewhere we can look at it together in one place and tell us which bike you are proposing for the window, and why.

The mark. This is the awkward part. The original artwork is gone. The person who drew it moved to Portugal and the studio that held the files closed in 2022. What we still have is: a photograph of the hand painted board that hangs over the bench, which carries the full wordmark with the flourish in two paint colours; a flatbed scan of an old letterhead, where the same wordmark is much smaller and flatter but printed cleanly in a single colour; and a close photograph of an enamel head badge on one of the frames. We need the mark back as proper artwork we can place at any size, from very small on a catalogue footer to very large on the shopfront glass, and we need to be told plainly which version belongs where and how small it can safely go.

The catalogue. Attached is last season's spec page as a PDF, which is all our previous designer left behind, and a spreadsheet of the eight builds with their specifications and prices. We want a printed spec book, one build to a page, laid out the same way as that PDF so it matches the folder our stockists already keep behind the counter, with each build's own photograph and its own numbers on its own page. We also want every page available on its own as a print ready file, so we can hand a single sheet to a customer who only cares about one bike. Fair warning on the spreadsheet: it was kept by three different people over two years and it shows, and not just in the formatting. Some of them wrote a component out in full and some wrote three letters, so the entries are nowhere near the same length. Make the eight pages read as one document.

The campaign. For opening week we need four things, and we want them to be four different pieces rather than the same picture cut four ways.

A full height graphic for the window beside the door, roughly 700 by 1000 millimetres. Somebody walks past that at about two metres, through glass, at walking pace. So: one bike sitting on a clean flat field, the mark, the opening line, nothing else. Not the workshop clutter that is behind it in the raw files.

A poster at A2 for the two cafes on the street who have offered to put one up. That one is read at arm's length by somebody with a coffee who has time, so it can be the opposite: close, quiet, detail. It should carry the address, the opening dates, the hours and the fitting session line.

A single page we can email to the local press and the cycling clubs with the story, the address and the hours set out properly so a listings editor can lift them straight off it.

And a set of posts for the feed: one square, one upright, one full screen vertical. Give each of the three something different to say and a different picture to say it with. We would rather three posts that each do one job than three crops of the same photograph.

One more thing. We have no photograph of anyone actually riding one of ours out on a street, and there is no time to shoot one before we open. If a general riding picture would strengthen the press page, source something properly licensed and tell us what it cost. It has to look like our street: a Northern European city on an ordinary damp day, brick or Bath stone, wet tarmac, somebody in normal clothes riding an upright unhurried bike. Not a race. No lycra, no carbon, no start line, no crowd, nobody wearing a number. And make it sit with the rest of our photography rather than looking bought in. Tell us what you turned down and why, so we know you looked properly.

Budget and tone. Framesets start at £1,650 and a complete build runs from £2,290 to £5,400. Our customers are mostly in their forties, they already own two or three bicycles, and this is usually the last one they intend to buy. So: quiet. No exclamation marks, no starbursts, no sale energy, no "from only". If it looks like it is trying to sell them something, we have lost them.

Delivery. We have one person in house, Marta, who can move a text box and change a price. She has an Adobe Express seat and she is the one who will send the window graphic to the sign maker and the poster to the printer, so what we need from you is the built document she can open and export from, plus the underlying source file so we are not stranded if something goes wrong with it. Next season we want to reprint the catalogue with new numbers without paying anybody. Please include a short written note telling us what you did to the photographs, why you chose the type, which version of the mark goes where, which pieces Marta exports herself and at what size, the licence cost of anything you bought, and what we should be careful of when we reuse this.
price_band_and_audience: Framesets from £1,650; complete builds £2,290 (Ashcott, steel audax build) to £5,400 (Clifton, polished stainless with a high end groupset); opening week carries a free fitting session rather than any discount. Buyers are 35 to 58, professional, already own two or three bicycles, buy once and keep it twenty years, and read a spec table properly. This band is load bearing on the design, not decoration: the price has to be earned by restraint, so it sits at body size in the text face with no rule beneath it and no currency emphasis, the window panel carries one bike on a held white field with more empty ground than graphic, the A2 poster is a close read on craft with the price absent entirely, the catalogue page gives the photograph generous margin instead of filling the trim, and a single starburst, drop shadow, exclamation mark or "from only" construction would relocate the whole kit into a £600 hybrid retailer's price band on sight. A £600 shop would set the price large and red; this one sets it small and grey. The band also decides the Stock frame: a rider in race kit on a carbon bike destroys a hand built steel audax brand at £2,290 more effectively than any typographic mistake could.

assets_supplied.name: thornbeck_builds.csv
assets_supplied.note: Eight rows, eleven columns, kept by three people over two years. Prices appear as '£2,290', '2290' and '2,290.00' in the same column; weights are mixed kilograms and pounds; sizes are 'S/M/L' on some rows and '52/54/56' on others; two model names carry a stray double space and several cells have trailing whitespace. Verbosity is wildly inconsistent between the three authors: the groupset cell reads 'Shimano 105 R7100 mechanical, 2x12, 50/34 with an 11-34 cassette' on three rows and '105 2x12' on others, and the tubing cell varies the same way. There is no image column at all, so nothing currently binds a build to its photograph.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Creative Cloud asset ingest and egress (asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT to the block transfer href, asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, asset_preview_file, asset_search, asset_get_presigned_urls)
adobe_surfaces.role: The only headless route by which any client file, any licensed Stock download and the authored HTML itself reach the imaging, InDesign and Express families, all three of which enforce their own domain whitelists and reject arbitrary public URLs. Also the channel through which the agent looks at its own outputs and at the finished Express document.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Lightroom and Photoshop imaging (image_auto_straighten, image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_adjustments, image_select_by_prompt, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize, image_vectorize plus local SVG hygiene)
adobe_surfaces.role: Level the knocked frame, normalise the ten frames, carry one shared house grade across daylight and tungsten so the eight bikes hold one white point and one black point when adjacent, resolve the split light frame through object bounded masks, keep a polished stainless flank separable from the wall behind it, cut the catalogue plates to the layout's true frame geometry at a shared subject scale, knock the window hero onto a clean white field with the frame triangle and wheel voids genuinely open, and recover the lost wordmark from two unlike sources down two opposite routes. Note that no Illustrator tool appears anywhere in this engagement: document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are on the dead async polling path and return no retrievable artifact headlessly, so all vector work is done through the Photoshop family vectorize path plus hand SVG hygiene, and that limitation is stated to the client.

Set the whole kit's type system. Two independent recommendation passes, one per typographic role, then the numeric OpenType weights per family, then one laundered kit embedded verbatim so the window, the poster, the press page, the social set and the specification page are typographically one thing. The pairing itself is unaided art direction; the tool refuses to pair. Typography control exists only on the Express surface, never on the InDesign surface, which is itself a constraint the agent must plan around.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout)
adobe_surfaces.role: Reverse engineer the client's flat price list PDF into a live merge template, bind the cleaned eight row CSV plus the agent produced per build photographs and a constant footer mark image, and deliver one press PDF at one build per page plus eight separately named single record sheets, then hand the template itself over so next season's reprint costs nothing.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express via HTML authoring (create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, export_html_to_express, asset_search CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview)
adobe_surfaces.role: Author the opening week collateral as one native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes in a single export: the window panel, the A2 cafe poster, the press one pager with a real hours table, three differently sourced social roots, and the mark and type specification page which is also where the small mark cut gets its dark ground test. Then look at what actually landed and correct it.

Source the one photograph the client cannot shoot before opening, a Northern European street riding frame at genuine camera scale and legally clean, art directed against an explicit reject list, then re-ingest it and pull it into the same house grade so it does not read as bought in beside the workshop set on the press page.

Stand up a persisted, shareable direction board. This is the first and only moment before the catalogue exists at which all ten graded masters sit adjacent, which is precisely where a grade that satisfies every frame individually is exposed as failing across the set. It is also where the agent records, in writing and against the assembled set, which build it commits to as the window hero and why.

trajectory.action: Upload all fourteen supplied files headlessly: asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT to the returned block transfer href, asset_finalize_file_upload, keeping each presignedAssetUrl.
trajectory.reasoning: Nothing in the imaging or InDesign families accepts an arbitrary public URL; they enforce their own domain whitelist, stricter than the Express importer's. Everything the client sent has to become an Adobe hosted presigned asset first or the engagement stalls at step two.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen presigned asset URLs: ten photographs, two logo sources, the price list PDF and the builds CSV.

trajectory.action: Call asset_inline_preview on every uploaded frame and both logo sources and actually look before touching anything. Sort the shoot into the daylight group and the tungsten group, find the tilted frame, find the split light frame, note where the speculars sit on the stainless and the chrome, and note that the eight bikes are not the same frame size and are not all the same distance from the wall. Separately, establish that the two logo sources are not the same problem and commit to one as primary: the painted board is the only source carrying the flourish and is the mark the client leads with, so it is the primary recovery target; the 900 pixel letterhead scan is triaged as a low value duplicate and parked.
trajectory.reasoning: The tool docs require a look before adjustment and crop calls, but the real reason is triage. The two logo sources look interchangeable in a file listing and are not: they are opposite recovery problems, one flat ink on white paper and one paint on timber shot off axis. Committing to the richer source is the correct first call on the evidence available now, and it is also the call that will have to be revisited later for a reason that does not exist yet.
trajectory.produces: A written triage: three cool frames, four warm, one split, one tilted, one stainless highlight risk, one bike further from the wall, two outlier frame sizes; and a stated decision to recover the mark from the painted board and park the scan.

trajectory.action: Run image_auto_straighten on the knocked frame so the floor line and skirting sit level, then image_apply_auto_tone across the ten frames as a normalisation pass only, not as the look.
trajectory.reasoning: Auto tone flattens the exposure spread between the daylight and tungsten halves so the single shared grade in the next step has something consistent to act on. Straightening has to happen before any crop, because a later crop would lock the tilt in permanently.
trajectory.produces: Ten levelled, exposure normalised intermediates.

trajectory.action: Apply one shared house grade with image_apply_adjustments over the normalised set: a cool neutral white point, a common black point, highlights pulled back so the stainless top tube specular and the chrome fork crown hold rather than clip, saturation restrained, and only the temperature offset varied between the daylight and tungsten sources so both land on the same neutral. The split light frame takes a single compromise white point at this stage and the agent says so rather than pretending otherwise. Report every parameter dialled.
trajectory.reasoning: This is the irreversible craft decision of the whole engagement. Every downstream deliverable is built on these masters, and once a warm or muddy plate is base64 inlined or bound into a merge it looks perfectly fine in isolation and only reads as broken where two bikes sit adjacent. Grading each frame until it looks nice on its own is the mistake, and it is the comfortable mistake.
trajectory.produces: Ten graded house masters intended to hold one white point and one black point, plus a written record of the parameters and of the compromise taken on the split light frame.

trajectory.action: boards_create_new_board, then boards_add_items_to_board with all ten graded masters in one call, staying inside the twelve placement cap and using presigned URLs rather than raw blobs. Confirm addedEntityIds are minted and failedItems is empty. Then look at the assembled board and, against the set rather than against any single frame, state in writing which build is committed as the window hero and why.
trajectory.reasoning: This is the first moment in the entire engagement at which all ten frames sit adjacent, and adjacency is the only condition under which the client's actual requirement, that a customer must not notice they were shot on different days, can be evaluated at all. It is also the honest place to fix the window hero, because that choice is a comparison, not a preference.
trajectory.produces: A live board URL with verified entity ids and zero failures, a committed window hero build, and one problem that was invisible on ten separate previews.

trajectory.action: Return to the grade. The compromise white point taken on the split light frame is wrong in a way only the assembled set reveals: it splits the difference, so the daylight front half now reads cooler than the seven daylight frames while the tungsten rear half still reads warmer than the four tungsten frames, and it is the only frame on the board matching nothing. Resolve it by binding the correction to objects rather than to light, since a prompt naming a geometric band or a lighting zone is a rejected framing. Select the rear wheel, the drivetrain and the saddle individually by prompt, composite those masks, and apply a temperature only offset through image_apply_adjustments with that maskURI while the shared house grade stays unmasked across the whole frame. Re-add the corrected frame to the board and look again. If the warm zone does not follow object boundaries closely enough to hide the transition, revert to a single compromise white point biased to the daylight group and report plainly that this was done and why.
trajectory.reasoning: A frame that matches nothing is worse than a frame that is slightly wrong in the same direction as its group, and that judgement is only available once the set exists in one place. The mechanism matters as much as the diagnosis: the obvious instinct is to select the warm half, and no selection tool in the family will accept that as a prompt.
trajectory.produces: A corrected split light master that now sits with the daylight group, the mask composition described, and a set of ten that survives adjacency.

trajectory.action: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset and a short generic query, filtered to contentType Photo, reading width and height for true full resolution and isGenTech to exclude AI generated frames. Shortlist against the client's stated street: a Northern European city on a damp ordinary day, brick or stone terrace, wet tarmac, a rider in normal clothes on an upright unhurried bike. Reject on sight anything with race kit, a carbon frame, a start line, a crowd or a rider number, and write down what was rejected and on which ground. License the pick with asset_license_and_download_stock and curl the presigned download immediately. Then re-ingest the downloaded JPEG through asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT, asset_finalize_file_upload to mint an Adobe hosted presigned asset URL.
trajectory.reasoning: Short queries are required because long ones return zero hits, and the orientation filter is broken and must never be passed. The re-ingest is not optional bookkeeping: the Stock download URL expires within the hour and its host is not on the imaging family's whitelist, so a downloaded local file cannot be graded until it has been uploaded back through the egress path. Downloading and then grading reads as complete and is not. The rejection list is the deliverable half of this step, because an unguarded search on this brief returns riders anywhere in the world in race kit, and that single wrong pick would price the brand at six hundred pounds.
trajectory.produces: One licensed street riding photograph at genuine camera scale on an Adobe hosted URL, its licence cost, and a written record of the candidates turned down and why.

trajectory.action: Pull the licensed frame into the same house grade: same white point, same black point, highlights held to the same ceiling, saturation restrained to match. Add it to the board as the eleventh item and check it against the workshop set.
trajectory.reasoning: A bought in photograph sitting next to nine house graded ones announces itself instantly through its warmth and its contrast curve. The client asked for it not to look bought in, and that is a grading problem, not a selection problem. Checking it on the board rather than alone is the same discipline that caught the split light frame.
trajectory.produces: The street frame graded into the house look and verified adjacent to the set; the board now carries eleven items.

trajectory.action: Run font_recommend once for the display role and once, independently, for the text role. Then font_styles on every shortlisted family to read the real numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder each chosen name into canonical PostScript form, and one get_fontkit_embed_url call carrying every face in the kit. Record the returned css_stack slugs and the numeric weights per role.
trajectory.reasoning: The tool deliberately refuses to pair, so the display and text pairing is entirely the agent's art direction, and it is where the price band gets encoded. The laundering matters because family name input is accepted at lookup and rejected at the embed step, and one bad name kills the entire kit including every valid face in it. The numeric weights are non standard per family, so the reflexive four hundred can ship Light and quietly collapse the hierarchy the price band depends on.
trajectory.produces: One Typekit embed carrying the whole type system, with the correct slug and the correct numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Recover the display cut of the mark from the painted board. The wordmark is two paint colours on timber, and selection is unreliably partial on compound marks, so run image_select_by_prompt twice: once naming the oxide red painted lettering by its colour, medium and form, once naming the off white painted flourish the same way. Look at both masks. Because the off white paint will not survive being flattened onto a white ground, first drop its lightness through its own mask with image_apply_adjustments so it stays separable, then composite the two masks, invert the union, lay a flat plate through the inverted mask with image_fill_area, crop to the returned bounding box and vectorize. Finish locally: inject a viewBox, delete the full canvas background path that vectorize always emits as path index zero, set the two recovered path groups to the brand oxide red and off white by hand, and verify by counting two distinct non background fills in the SVG.
trajectory.reasoning: Naming the substrate rather than the graphic pulls the selection to the timber and returns a board shaped blob that still reports success and poisons everything downstream. The two colour problem is real and the tools do not solve it for you: vectorize takes no options at all, so every separation decision has to be made in the raster prep, and an off white stroke laid on a white ground simply is not there afterwards. Setting the final hues by hand in the SVG is what a designer actually does; the vectorize only has to produce separable geometry.
trajectory.produces: A colour true display cut of the wordmark carrying the flourish, with a viewBox, no background rectangle and two verified distinct fills, plus the pre vectorize raster plate on a presigned URL.

trajectory.action: convert_pdf_to_indd on last season's price list, then export_idml on the result, then download and unzip the IDML and read the real document. Record how many text frames actually exist and whether the spec copy converted as one continuous story or as separate blocks; reconstruct each frame's true story text by concatenating every Content run in the story XML rather than trusting the mapping tool's reported text, which is known to drop whole runs while keeping their line breaks; read the true bounds and aspect of the product photograph frame; and confirm the footer mark converted as a graphics frame with its own integer page item id and a link resource URI, which is what makes it swappable at all.
trajectory.reasoning: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control, and a continuous flow collapses into a single text frame that has to be mapped by offset rather than per field. The IDML round trip is not a fallback here, it is the mandatory first move, because the mapping tool's reported text is lossy and every offset computed from it will be wrong by a fixed amount while still validating cleanly. Doing this before any crop is the difference between cutting the photography once and cutting it twice: the frame's aspect is knowable here and nowhere earlier.
trajectory.produces: A converted .indd, an IDML, the true reconstructed story text, the photograph frame's real near square aspect and fitting behaviour, and the footer mark's page item id.

trajectory.action: Cut the eight bike masters for the catalogue at the photograph frame's true near square aspect learned from the IDML. Run image_select_subject with returnBbox on each bike, read metadata.detection_confidence and fall back to an explicit prompt driven selection where it sits below roughly 0.6, then image_crop_to_bounds on the returned bounds padded by a fixed percentage of each bike's own bounding box. Upload the eight cut plates.
trajectory.reasoning: Cutting to the layout's real geometry rather than to the 3:2 camera frame is the whole reason the IDML was read first. Padding each crop by a percentage of its own subject is the obvious and defensible first rule, and it is what a competent person does with no page to look at yet.
trajectory.produces: Eight catalogue plates at the frame's true aspect, uploaded, plus one selection that behaved badly enough to be worth chasing.

trajectory.action: Return to the grade for the polished stainless build. Its subject selection came back clipping the top tube, because the graded polish on the tube's flank now sits at close to the same value as the pale grey wall directly behind it, and the mask simply stopped where it could no longer tell them apart. Do not fix this by hand padding the bounds, which would leave that one plate cropped off centre against seven that are not. Fix it upstream with a masked local move: select the frame tubing by prompt and lift local contrast through that mask with image_apply_adjustments, leaving the frame's white point and black point untouched so it does not drift away from the set, then re-check it on the board and re-run the selection and crop.
trajectory.reasoning: The grade's highlight ceiling was set to hold the specular and it does; what it also did, invisibly, was flatten the tube toward the wall value, and that is only discoverable when a selection tool tries to separate the two. A global correction would move this frame off the shared white point and reintroduce exactly the consistency problem the grade exists to solve, so the correction has to be regional and the reasoning has to be about the set, not about the frame.
trajectory.produces: A stainless master that separates cleanly from its background, still holding the house white and black point, and a correct eighth catalogue plate.

trajectory.action: Clean the CSV locally: normalise the three price formats to one, convert every weight to a single unit, resolve the two size schemes into one, strip trailing whitespace and the stray double spaces in the model names. Add an at prefixed image column holding the bare filename of each build's own cut plate, and a second at prefixed constant column holding the same footer mark filename on all eight rows.
trajectory.reasoning: The merge binds on exact strings, so mixed formats do not fail loudly, they just print inconsistently across eight pages. Neither image column exists in the supplied file at all, so without adding them every page carries the same static photograph and the same footer graphic the previous designer left in the PDF, which is the classic silent failure of this job.
trajectory.produces: A clean eight row merge CSV with a working per build image column and a constant mark column.

trajectory.action: generate_indd_mapping_prompt against the IDML and the cleaned CSV to get the integer page item ids and bounds, then build the mappings with every text offset computed against the reconstructed true story text from step 11 rather than the tool's reported content. Use replace_text and insert_at_position, never replace_all, for text; list insert rows sharing a uid in descending position order against the original string. Map the per build photograph and the constant footer mark as image mappings, where replace_all is legitimate. Pass the mapping back through the same tool as a validator.
trajectory.reasoning: The uid has to be the integer page item id rather than the IDML self string or the row is silently dropped. The validator is worth running but it is not evidence: it returns valid on offsets computed from lossy text without a single warning, which is exactly why the offsets came from the document itself.
trajectory.produces: A mapping covering seven text fields plus two image frames, reported valid.

trajectory.action: prepare_indd_merge_template with the converted .indd, the cleaned CSV, and the whole mapping passed as a single JSON string in params rather than as flat parameters. Then export_idml on the result and grep the stories for all seven expected placeholders, and confirm the footer frame's link resource URI has actually changed.
trajectory.reasoning: Splitting the mapping across flat parameters means whole arrays are never read by the server script; one stringified object is the only reliable shape. And a success message from prepare is not evidence of anything, so the round trip is run again here to prove the placeholders are physically present before a single record is merged.
trajectory.produces: A merge template with all seven placeholders confirmed present in the round tripped IDML and both image frames confirmed rebound.

trajectory.action: Prove one record before committing: document_merge_data_layout with recordRange set to a single row, output to InDesign format, then document_render_layout at 300 DPI, then actually look at the rendered page.
trajectory.reasoning: Every response so far has said success, and none of them looked at a page. Rendering one record at true print resolution costs almost nothing and is the only place the template's real behaviour becomes visible before eight pages of it exist. Note that resolution passed to the merge call itself is silently ignored and returns 72 DPI, so real print resolution only exists through the render step.
trajectory.produces: One 300 DPI single record proof page, and two defects visible on it that no tool response reported.

trajectory.action: Return to the mapping. The starting price prints in the italic caption face at caption size, on a page where every other number is body weight, because the offset chosen for it lands inside the run belonging to the preceding lead in word and the inserted placeholder inherited that run's character style. Re-anchor it: replace a target string that lies wholly inside the correctly styled body run instead of inserting at a position that straddles the boundary. Re-validate, re-prepare, re-export the IDML to confirm the placeholder is still present, and re-proof the single record.
trajectory.reasoning: The mandatory IDML round trip proves that a placeholder exists; it says nothing at all about which character style it inherited, and nothing in the validator, the prepare response or the merge response mentions style. Only a rendered page shows it. On this brief the defect is not cosmetic: the price is the one element the whole design is built to underplay, and setting it in a different face from the rest of the numbers is precisely the loud, cheap gesture the price band forbids.
trajectory.produces: A corrected mapping and a re proofed record where the price sits at body size in the text face.

trajectory.action: Return to the vector stage and unpark the letterhead scan. At true 300 DPI the footer mark, sitting at roughly fourteen millimetres wide, does not hold: the display cut recovered from the painted board carries brush texture and hairline strokes that fill in and break up at that size. Build the second cut down the opposite route, because the scan is flat dark ink on white paper rather than paint on timber: select the printed lettering by prompt, invert the selection for correct polarity, and crop to the returned bounds. Take two artifacts off that route. The cropped raster plate, at its native cropped resolution of roughly seven hundred pixels, is the footer graphic for InDesign, comfortably above the hundred and sixty five pixels that fourteen millimetres at 300 DPI actually needs. Vectorize the same plate, strip path zero and inject a viewBox, and that SVG is the small size cut for Express. State a minimum reproduction width for it. Rebind the constant mark column to the new filename, re-prepare, and re-proof.
trajectory.reasoning: Print scale is the only condition under which this is visible. At document zoom on screen the display cut looks correct at any size, and no tool reports anything. It also settles the question the client asked in writing, which is which version goes where, and the honest answer turns out to be that the source triaged as a low value duplicate at step two is the only one that works small. Note that there is no vector to raster tool anywhere in the connector and no route for placing an SVG into an InDesign frame, so the catalogue necessarily carries the raster cut and the client is told so.
trajectory.produces: A simplified single colour mark in two forms, a raster footer plate bound into the template and an SVG small cut for Express, each with a stated minimum reproduction width, and a clean re proofed footer.

trajectory.action: Run the full merge across all eight records with the per build images bound through the at prefixed column and the additional image files map keyed to the exact bare filenames. Take two branches off it: merge once to PDF for a single press file at one build per page, and merge once to InDesign format then document_render_layout with separate files for eight one page PDFs, naming each to its build on download. Then lay the eight pages out and read them as a set, which is how the stockist will.
trajectory.reasoning: Merging to a raster media type ignores the requested resolution and silently returns 72 DPI, and multi record raster URLs come back in reversed order with labels that lie, so per record identity is only safe through the PDF and separate files routes, both of which are verified to hold CSV order. A single sheet handed to a customer wants to be a PDF anyway.
trajectory.produces: One eight page press PDF plus eight correctly named single record sheets, and two problems that only exist once eight pages sit together.

trajectory.action: Return to the CSV. On two of the eight builds the spec copy sets several lines deeper than the rest and runs into the photograph area, because the previous designer's placeholder text was his own terse specimen copy and two of the three people who kept the spreadsheet wrote their components out in full while the third abbreviated. This is an editorial fix, not a layout one: normalise the spec copy depth across all eight rows to one house voice and one level of detail, keeping every number the client actually stated, then re-merge and re-render both branches.
trajectory.reasoning: The template's frame depths were set against copy nobody in this engagement wrote, so no inspection of the template before the merge could have shown this. It is also not fixable in the layout, since the connector offers no free form frame editing at all: the only lever is the data. And leaving two pages typographically deeper than the other six fails the client's actual stated ask, which was that the eight pages read as one document.
trajectory.produces: A normalised CSV and an eight page set that sets to one depth.

trajectory.action: Return to the crop stage and re-cut all eight. Read across the eight rendered pages and the bicycles sit at eight different scales inside an identical frame: the 58 fills its frame, the 52 floats in it, and the bike that was further from the wall reads smaller than either. Padding each crop by a percentage of its own subject produced exactly that, because it preserved each bike's own proportions rather than a shared one. Re-cut to a common scale reference instead, padding each subject bounding box so the wheelbase reads at a consistent proportion of the frame width across the whole set. Read detection_confidence on every selection, and where a resize rather than a pure crop is needed read metadata.upscale_factor and the tradeoffs array and reject any result carrying an upscaled entry. Re-upload, rebind the image column, re-merge and re-render both branches.
trajectory.reasoning: Every page passes on its own; the set does not, and eight rendered pages side by side is the only place that can be seen. It is also the same discipline failure as the grade, one stage later and in geometry instead of colour, which is why it cannot be fixed in the layout and has to be remade in the image editor. The tradeoff reading has to be split by tool: a crop to bounds cannot upscale and reports no upscale factor, but a crop and resize interpolates silently to a hard two times cap and announces it only in an array that is easy to ignore.
trajectory.produces: Eight re-cut catalogue plates at a shared subject scale, none interpolated, rebound and re-rendered into the final press PDF and the eight named sheets.

trajectory.action: Cut the committed window hero out of its workshop surroundings onto a clean flat white field with image_remove_background carrying a white background colour, then crop for the window canvas. Read the tradeoffs array for a downscaled entry and record the actual output dimensions.
trajectory.reasoning: The client asked for one bike on a clean field with nothing behind it, and the graded masters all carry a bench, a parts bin and a hose. Compositing the subject straight onto a solid ground in one call is the direct and verified route, and it is what the tool exists for. The downscale reading is not optional: this tool quietly shrinks oversized inputs and reports it nowhere else, and the window is the deliverable whose stated effective resolution at printed size depends on it.
trajectory.produces: A first hero plate on a white field with its true output dimensions recorded, ready to inline.

trajectory.action: Load the authoring playbook, then downsample every photograph to no more than the pixels it actually occupies on its destination canvas, reading the tradeoffs array to confirm each operation is downward only, and base64 inline each one. Author one self contained multi root HTML document with seven roots, each declaring its own canvas size: the window panel at 350 by 500 millimetres as a declared half scale artboard of the 700 by 1000 piece; the A2 cafe poster at 210 by 297 millimetres, also half scale, carrying the graded lug macro with the enamel head badge as its image and the address, opening dates, hours and fitting line as its copy, with no price anywhere on it; the press one pager at A4 with the graded licensed street frame as its lead image and the opening hours set as a real table a listings editor can read off; a 1080 square carrying the graded workshop wide on the line about the workshop being visible from the pavement; a 1080 by 1350 carrying the graded lug macro at close read with no price; a 1080 by 1920 carrying the window hero on its white field with the opening date; and a mark and type specification page showing both cuts at their intended sizes with minimum widths and clear space, with the small cut placed as inline SVG on a dark panel. Paste the font kit embed verbatim, set family from the returned slug and the numeric weight explicitly on every text element, wrap every inline SVG in a container with explicit position and explicit width and height, anchor everything from the left and top, and set the page ground to the same white the hero was composited onto.
trajectory.reasoning: A photograph referenced by URL returns HTTP success and renders as an empty grey box, and that holds even for the connector's own asset hosts, so data URIs are the only route that works. Inlining at camera scale would put the payload far past anything measured, which is the same no waste discipline the no upscale rule already imposes in the other direction. Right anchored and content sized wrappers collapse and throw inline SVG off the canvas edge. Passing canvas dimensions as tool parameters would suppress the per root sizes and flatten the mixed canvas set into one size. Half scale artboards are ordinary large format practice and they keep the biggest root near the verified envelope while making the effective resolution at final printed size a checkable number rather than an assertion. The dark panel on the specification page is where the small cut gets its dark ground test, since there is no way to rasterize an SVG in this connector and no other dark ground in the kit.
trajectory.produces: One multi root HTML source carrying every opening week canvas at a controlled payload size.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, then, because seven roots of inlined photography put the payload far past the inline threshold, upload the HTML itself as an asset and pass its Adobe hosted presigned URL to the exporter rather than sending it inline.
trajectory.reasoning: The readiness step is mandatory before every export and every retry, and the importer only accepts HTML from a small set of hosts, so routing a heavy payload through the asset upload path is a planned decision rather than a discovery. If the oversized window root is rejected or flattens the mixed canvas set to one size, fall back to exporting the window panel as its own single root document and say so.
trajectory.produces: One native editable Express document with the expected slide count and per root canvas sizes.

trajectory.action: Verify rather than assume. Find the produced document by asset search, resolve its rendition and preview it to see the first artboard rendered, and parse the returned per root HzHTML for the resolved PostScript faces, the image fills, the table structure and the per root dimensions on the roots the preview cannot show.
trajectory.reasoning: Every failure on this surface returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard, so the remaining roots have to be checked through the returned markup. This is the only honest way to know whether the type took or silently fell back to a default sans, and it is also the only way the window panel gets looked at on a clean ground at size.
trajectory.produces: A verification record per root, and one defect on the window panel that was invisible everywhere upstream.

trajectory.action: Return to the hero cutout and take the other route. On the white window field the plate reads as a bike shaped slab: subject based removal cannot punch an enclosed interior, so the pale workshop wall stayed trapped inside the main frame triangle and inside both wheels. Invert the approach. Run image_select_subject on the graded master with returnBbox, invert that selection, and lay the flat white through the inverted mask with image_fill_area on the original. Everything that is not the bicycle, including the wall, the floor, the bench, the parts bin, the hose and every pixel visible through the frame triangle and both wheels, becomes one ground in a single call. If the subject mask comes back partial across the spokes or the bars, which compound subject selection is known to do, fall back to selecting the painted wall and the concrete floor as material fields, composite those masks with a bench and bin selection so the clutter is included, and fill through that instead. Read the tradeoffs for a downscaled entry and record the output dimensions again. Re-crop for the window and the vertical social root, re-downsample, re-inline as fresh data URIs, re-run the readiness check, re-export and re-verify both roots.
trajectory.reasoning: This is invisible against the original workshop background and invisible in the raw file, and it only becomes obvious once the plate sits on a clean flat ground at shopfront height. A bicycle is the worst case for any isolation workflow precisely because it is mostly holes, and the fix is a change of polarity rather than a change of effort. The material field route is the fallback rather than the primary because the bench, the bin and the hose are neither wall nor floor and would survive a wall and floor fill, leaving workshop objects floating in the clean field on the single most public piece in the launch.
trajectory.produces: A corrected hero plate with genuinely open frame and wheel voids and no surviving workshop objects, re-inlined, and the final verified Express document.

trajectory.action: Write the client note and package the source. Cover the grade parameters actually applied and how the split light frame and the stainless frame were each handled regionally rather than globally; the display and text pairing with the reasoning and the correct numeric weights; which mark cut belongs at which size, with the stated minimum reproduction width for the small cut and a plain statement that vector artwork cannot be placed into the InDesign catalogue through this route so the footer carries the raster cut; the merge field map, the cleaned CSV and how to reprint next season against new numbers; the Stock licence, its cost and the candidates rejected and why; which pieces Marta exports herself out of Express, at what size, and that the window and poster artboards are half scale with the effective resolution at final printed size stated; and a plain statement that no output anywhere exceeds its source resolution. Hand over the authored HTML source alongside the Express document.
trajectory.reasoning: The client has one person in house who can change a price, an Express seat, and a stated intention to reprint without paying anybody. The handover is what makes the merge template and the Express document a working system rather than a set of files, and the HTML source is the only durable, portable, re-openable form of those canvases given that nothing in this connector can export a file out of an Express document.
trajectory.produces: The written handover note, the authored HTML source, the reusable merge template and its field map, and the specification page living inside the Express document.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: With all ten graded masters assembled on one board for the first time, the split light frame is the only one in the set that matches nothing. The compromise white point applied to it in the shared grade splits the difference between its daylight front half and its tungsten rear half, so its front now reads cooler than the seven daylight frames while its rear still reads warmer than the four tungsten frames. On its own preview it looks acceptably neutral, which is why it passed the grade step, and no tool reported anything.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: Go back to the grade and bind the correction to objects instead of to light, because a prompt naming a lighting zone or a geometric band is a rejected framing that no selection tool will accept. Select the rear wheel, the drivetrain and the saddle individually by prompt, composite those masks, and apply a temperature only offset through the mask while the shared house grade stays unmasked over the whole frame. If the warm zone does not follow object boundaries closely enough to hide the transition, take a single compromise white point biased toward the daylight group and report that this was done.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: One of the eight floor bikes reads as a different bike shop on every surface it appears on, and it is the only frame that cannot be excused as being slightly warm or slightly cool with its group. The client's single stated requirement of the photography, that a customer must not notice they were shot on different days, fails on the page that shows the range.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: Subject selection on the polished stainless build comes back clipping the top tube. The house grade's highlight ceiling, set deliberately to hold the full length specular, also flattened the tube's polished flank toward the value of the pale grey wall directly behind it, and the mask stopped where it could no longer tell them apart. Nothing about the graded frame looks wrong; the specular is held exactly as intended. The defect only exists as a consequence of a downstream tool trying to separate two things the grade made similar.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: Do not hand pad the bounds, which fixes this plate at the cost of cropping it off centre against seven that are not. Go back to the grade and make a regional move: select the frame tubing by prompt and lift local contrast through that mask, leaving the frame's white point and black point untouched so it does not drift off the shared neutral, then re-check it on the board and re-run the selection and the crop.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: Either the most expensive build in the range, the five thousand four hundred pound flagship, ships with its top tube sliced through on the catalogue page, or it ships hand padded and visibly differently composed from the other seven. A global contrast correction, the other tempting fix, moves it off the house white point and reintroduces the exact consistency failure the whole grade exists to prevent.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The single record proof at true 300 DPI shows the starting price set in the italic caption face at caption size while every other number on the page is body weight. Every check upstream passed: the offsets were computed from the reconstructed true story text rather than the mapping tool's lossy report, the validator returned valid, prepare reported success, the round tripped IDML confirmed all seven placeholders physically present, and the merge ran clean. Placeholder presence is what the mandatory round trip proves; character style inheritance at the insertion point is not, and nothing in any response mentions it.

The offset chosen for it lands inside the run belonging to the preceding lead in word, so the inserted placeholder inherited that run's character style. Replace a target string that lies wholly inside the correctly styled body run instead of inserting at a position that straddles the run boundary, then re-validate, re-prepare, re-confirm the placeholder in the IDML and re-proof the record.

On this brief that is not a cosmetic slip: the price is the single element the entire design is built to underplay, and typographically singling it out is precisely the loud, cheap gesture that relocates a five thousand pound frame builder into a discount retailer's band. The client discovers it at the printer, because every tool response along the way said success.

The display cut taken off the painted board carries brush texture and hairline strokes that fill in and break up at that size. There is no signal for this anywhere on screen at document zoom, and the step two triage that committed to the painted board and parked the letterhead scan as a low value duplicate was correct on the evidence then available: it is the only source carrying the flourish and it is the mark the client leads with.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: Go back to the vector stage and unpark the scan, running the opposite recovery route on it because it is flat dark ink on white paper rather than paint on timber: select the printed lettering by prompt, invert for polarity, crop to bounds. Take two artifacts off that route, since there is no vector to raster tool in the connector and no way to place an SVG into an InDesign frame: the cropped raster plate becomes the footer graphic bound through the constant image column, and the vectorized version becomes the small size SVG cut for the Express roots. Strip path zero, inject a viewBox, state a minimum reproduction width, rebind, re-prepare and re-proof.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: Every one of the eight catalogue pages carries a muddy, partly filled mark in the footer, which is the one element on the page that is supposed to be the recovered brand asset. It also fails a requirement the client stated in writing, which was to be told which version belongs where and how small it can safely go, since shipping one cut for all sizes answers that question wrongly.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: With all eight pages rendered and laid out as a set, two of them set several lines deeper than the other six and the spec copy runs into the photograph area. The template's frame depths were set by the previous designer against his own terse specimen copy, and the client's real entries were written by three different people, two of whom spelled every component out in full while the third abbreviated. No inspection of the template before the merge could have shown this, because the copy that overruns is the client's, not the template's.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: Return to the data and fix it editorially rather than mechanically. The connector offers no free form frame editing of any kind, so the only lever is the CSV: normalise the spec copy across all eight rows to one house voice and one level of detail, keeping every number the client actually stated, then re-merge and re-render both delivery branches.

The temptation is to shrink the type on those two records, which is not possible here and would be wrong anyway, since it would make two pages typographically different from six in order to hide that they already are.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: Read across the eight rendered pages, the bicycles sit at eight different scales inside an identical frame. The 58 fills its frame, the 52 floats in it, and the bike that was shot further from the wall reads smaller than either. Read detection confidence on every selection, and wherever a resize rather than a pure crop is needed read the upscale factor and the tradeoffs array and reject anything reporting interpolation. Re-upload the eight, rebind the image column, re-merge and re-render both branches.

It is the same discipline failure as the grade, one stage later and in geometry rather than colour, and like the grade it cannot be corrected in the layout because there is no free form layout control at all; it has to be remade in the image editor and rebound.

Compositing the subject onto a solid ground in one call is the verified, direct route and it succeeded, but it cannot punch an enclosed interior, so the pale grey workshop wall stayed trapped inside the main frame triangle and inside both wheel voids. Against the original workshop background this is invisible; in the raw file it is invisible; on a clean white field at shopfront height it is the first thing anyone sees.
