Select the subject with a bounding box, invert that selection, and lay the flat white through the inverted mask on the original, so everything that is not the bicycle, including the wall, the floor, the bench, the parts bin, the hose and every pixel visible through the frame triangle and both wheels, becomes one ground in a single call. Keep the material field route, selecting the painted wall and the concrete floor and compositing them with a bench and bin selection, only as the stated fallback for when the subject mask comes back partial across the spokes or the bars. Re-crop, re-downsample, re-inline as fresh data URIs, re-run the mandatory readiness check and re-export.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The 700 by 1000 millimetre window graphic, the single most public piece in the launch and the first thing anyone walking down Redcliffe Street sees, shows a bicycle with a grey panel where the frame triangle should be open and two grey discs where the wheels should be, at full shopfront height. The vertical social root, which shares the same plate, carries the identical defect.

deliverables.name: Thornbeck house graded masters and direction board
deliverables.spec: Ten photographs from the workshop shoot plus the licensed street frame, all brought to one house look: one white point, one black point, highlights held so the stainless top tube specular and the chrome fork crown do not clip, the deep green frame back to green without dragging the neutrals, the knocked frame levelled, the split light frame resolved through composited object masks rather than one global move, and the stainless frame given a regional contrast lift so it stays separable from the wall without leaving the shared neutral. Delivered with the parameters applied, reported rather than measured, alongside the persisted board URL carrying all eleven frames with verified entity ids and zero failed items, on which the window hero was chosen against the assembled set. No output exceeds its source resolution.

deliverables.name: Window hero cutout plate
deliverables.spec: One hero bicycle, named to the build committed on the direction board, isolated onto a clean flat white field for the window panel and reused on the vertical social root, with the main frame triangle and both wheel voids genuinely open rather than filled with captured workshop wall, and with the bench, the parts bin and the hose gone rather than left floating in the field. Cropped for each canvas at native resolution with no interpolation, the tradeoffs array read for any silent downscale, the actual output dimensions recorded, and the effective resolution at final printed size stated.

deliverables.name: Thornbeck recovered mark system
deliverables.spec: Two cuts of the recovered wordmark. A colour true display cut carrying the flourish, recovered from the painted board through two separate colour prompts composited before flattening, with the oxide red and off white surviving as two verified distinct fills, for the shopfront glass and the specification page. And a simplified single colour cut recovered from the letterhead scan for small sizes, shipped in two forms because no vector to raster tool exists and no SVG can be placed into an InDesign frame: a raster plate at roughly seven hundred pixels bound into the catalogue footer, and an SVG for the Express roots. Both SVGs carry an injected viewBox and have the opaque full canvas background path removed. Each ships with a stated minimum reproduction width and a note on which grounds it is safe against, with the small cut tested on the dark panel of the specification page.

deliverables.name: Thornbeck 2026 spec book
deliverables.spec: One press PDF, eight pages, one build per page, page count equal to CSV row count, built on a live merge template reverse engineered from the client's own flat price list PDF so it matches the folder the stockists already hold. All seven data fields present on every page and confirmed in the round tripped IDML, the price set at body size in the text face rather than inheriting the caption italic, each build bound to its own re-cut photograph through the image column at a shared subject scale across the set, the footer carrying the small mark cut, and the spec copy normalised so all eight pages set to one depth. Plus eight separately named single record one page PDFs in verified CSV order, one per build, for handing to a customer interested in one bike.

deliverables.name: Thornbeck reusable merge template and field map
deliverables.spec: The live InDesign merge template itself plus the cleaned, normalised eight row CSV and the written field map, handed over so the client's in house person can reprint next season against new numbers without redoing the PDF reverse engineering. This is a production instrument rather than a merged output, and on the client's own stated terms it is the most valuable thing in the engagement.

deliverables.name: Opening week campaign set
deliverables.spec: One native editable Adobe Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes in a single export, seven roots, each doing a different job with a different source. A window panel authored at declared half scale for the 700 by 1000 millimetre piece, carrying the hero on white with the display mark and the opening line and nothing else. An A2 cafe poster, also half scale, built on the graded lug macro and the enamel head badge as a close read piece carrying address, opening dates, hours and the fitting line, with no price on it. A press and clubs one pager at A4 whose lead image is the graded licensed street frame, with the opening hours set as a real editable table. Three social roots at 1080 by 1080, 1080 by 1350 and 1080 by 1920 built respectively on the graded workshop wide, the graded lug macro and the window hero, so consistency is testable three separate ways rather than once. And a mark and type specification root. One type system across every root at the correct non standard numeric weights, both mark cuts placed as native editable vector, every photograph rendering as real pixels rather than an empty box, and the authored self contained HTML source handed over alongside it as the durable portable form, since nothing in this connector can export a file out of an Express document.

deliverables.name: Written handover note
deliverables.spec: A written note covering the grade parameters applied and why the split light and stainless frames were each handled regionally rather than globally, the display and text pairing with its reasoning and the correct numeric weights per family, which mark cut goes where with the stated minimum width and the vector into InDesign limitation stated plainly, the merge field map and reprint instructions against the handed over template, the Stock licence with its cost and the candidates rejected and on which grounds, which pieces the client exports herself out of Express and at what size including the half scale artboards and their effective resolution at final printed size, and a plain statement that nothing was upscaled. The mark and type specification page is a root of the Express document, not a separate deliverable, and is referenced from here. Honest artifact class count for the engagement is six distinct classes, which is well clear of the three class floor without inflating a specification page or a template into classes of their own.

decision_gates: The shared house grade set before anything else is irreversible downstream. A plate that is a touch warm or a touch muddy looks entirely acceptable on its own and only reads as broken where two bikes sit adjacent, so a non designer grades each frame until it looks nice individually and thereby guarantees eight bikes that do not match. The corollary gate is that the compromise chosen for the split light frame can only be judged against the assembled set, where splitting the difference is revealed as the one choice that matches nothing.

A grade decision can break a mechanical dependency, not just a visual one. Holding the specular on the polished stainless flattened it toward the wall value, and the failure surfaces as a subject selection that clips the top tube. The gate is recognising that hand padding the bounds fixes the symptom and ruins the set, and that the correct fix is a regional contrast move that leaves the white point and black point alone.

The two logo sources look like the same job in a file listing and need opposite treatments. The flat letterhead scan wants the lettering selected and the polarity inverted before vectorizing. The painted board wants prompts naming the graphic's own colour, medium and form, because naming the board pulls the selection to the timber and returns a board shaped blob that still reports success. It is also two paint colours, not one, and flattening an off white stroke onto a white ground erases it, so the mark needs two composited selections and a lightness move before it can survive being vectorized at all.

One mark cut cannot serve both the shopfront glass and a fourteen millimetre footer, and the source correctly deprioritised at triage turns out to be the only one that works small. The judgement is that the brush texture which makes the display cut good at a metre is precisely what kills it at fourteen millimetres, that this has no on screen signal at all, and that the small cut has to ship as both a raster and a vector because there is no rasterizer in the connector and no route from SVG into an InDesign frame.

Cutting a bicycle onto a clean field is not a background removal problem, because a bicycle is mostly enclosed holes. Compositing the subject onto a solid ground succeeds and leaves the wall trapped inside the frame triangle and both wheels, and the defect is invisible until the plate lands on a flat ground at window size. The correct move is to invert the polarity and fill through the inverted subject mask, which also takes out the bench, the bin and the hose that a wall and floor material fill would leave floating.

Four consecutive success responses are not evidence. The mandatory IDML round trip proves a placeholder is physically present and says nothing about which character style it inherited, so a field can validate, prepare, merge and render while set in the wrong face. The judgement is knowing what a given verification actually verifies, and looking at a rendered page for the rest.

The crop rule is a set level decision, not a per image one. Padding each bounding box by a percentage of its own subject is defensible, faithful and wrong, because it reproduces the differences between a 52 and a 58 rather than resolving them, and the failure only exists across eight adjacent pages. It cannot be fixed in the layout, because there is no free form layout control anywhere in this connector.

When a fixed layout cannot hold the client's real copy, the only available lever is the data, and using it correctly is editorial work rather than mechanical cleaning. The gate is normalising eight rows written by three people to one voice and one level of detail while keeping every number the client actually stated, rather than truncating cells or trying to reach into a frame the connector will not let anybody touch.

Photography referenced by URL returns HTTP success and renders as an empty grey box in the finished Express document, including from the connector's own asset hosts. Every photograph has to be pulled down and base64 inlined, downsampled first to the pixels it actually occupies, and the resulting payload routed through an asset upload rather than sent inline. Doing that as a plan rather than as a discovery is the difference between one export and three.

The type pairing is unassisted art direction, and the numeric weights are non standard per family, so writing the reflexive four hundred can ship Light and collapse the editorial hierarchy the price band depends on. At this band the price must sit at body size with no emphasis, which a non designer will instinctively reverse, and which the merge template will also reverse for you if the mapping offset lands in the wrong run.

The Stock pick is art direction under a hard positioning constraint, not a search. A rider in race kit on a carbon bike at a start line is the single fastest way to reprice a hand built steel audax brand downward, and the search is unguarded by default: short generic queries are required, the orientation filter is broken and returns nothing, and the download expires within the hour on a host the imaging tools reject, so a frame that is not immediately re-ingested cannot be graded at all.

The reprint requirement means the deliverable is not the eight pages, it is the template that makes the eight pages, plus the cleaned data and the field map. Merging once and handing over flat PDFs satisfies the visible ask and fails the actual one. The same logic applies on the Express side, where no file can be exported through the connector at all, so the authored HTML source is part of the handover rather than a working file.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and what comes back is unshippable on all three counts. Identity: the client needs their eight actual bicycles, correctly and consistently colour managed across two lighting conditions, and their actual wordmark, recovered from a painted board and a letterhead scan. A regenerated mark is not the mark, and the entire point of the recovery is that the original artwork no longer exists anywhere on earth. A plausible steel bicycle is worth nothing to a shop with eight specific ones on the floor. Spec: eight CSV rows must become exactly eight pages, each bound to its own photograph and its own seven numbers, plus eight separately named single record files in verified row order, plus a window panel at 700 by 1000 millimetres, an A2 poster, an A4 press page with a real table and three exact social canvases in one document. A one shot generation invents prices, invents specifications, hits none of the dimensions and cannot produce a page count equal to a row count. Editability: the client has one person in house who can move a text box, an Adobe Express seat, and a stated requirement to reprint next season with new numbers without paying anybody, which means the deliverable is a live merge template plus a cleaned CSV plus a native editable Express document plus its HTML source, not a flat raster. And the failure the client would actually notice first is the one no regeneration can even represent: consistency. Eight bikes at one white point and one black point and one subject scale, a mark that is the same mark at fourteen millimetres and at a metre, and one type system across seven canvases. Nothing about identity, exact record and page counts, cross asset consistency or downstream editability survives a regeneration.
doability_proof: Every step maps to a tool verified live on 2026-09-10, and no banned capability appears anywhere. Ingest: asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT to the block transfer href, asset_finalize_file_upload is verified fully headless with no file picker, and it is the only route into the imaging and InDesign families, both of which enforce their own domain whitelists. It is used three times deliberately: for the fourteen client files, for the licensed Stock JPEG after its S3 download (whose host the imaging tools reject and whose URL expires in one hour, so downloading is not the same as having it), and for the authored HTML itself. Imaging: image_auto_straighten, image_apply_auto_tone and image_apply_adjustments are verified, apply_adjustments accepts a maskURI for every region confined move, and the ten frame batch is exactly the documented ten image cap. image_select_by_prompt and image_select_subject with returnBbox give the only geometric readout in the family and drive image_crop_to_bounds. Material and texture selection by prompt is explicitly verified, which legitimises the stated fallback route on the hero. Compound mark selection being unreliably partial is documented, which is why the painted board is recovered through two composited prompts rather than one, and why the spec does not assert an outcome a single prompt cannot reach. image_fill_area accepts a maskURI and its verified options shape is preset white with opacity, so the ground colour is white throughout and the Express canvas ground is set to match rather than being left to chance. The naive hero route, image_remove_background with a backgroundColor, is verified to work and separately verified to fail on enclosed interiors, which is precisely why the seventh loop exists. Vector: image_vectorize is verified, takes no options at all, always emits a full canvas background rect as path zero and omits the viewBox, and both defects are fixed locally, which is the vector hygiene deliverable. No Illustrator tool appears anywhere, correctly, since document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on the dead vectorPollingHelper path and return no retrievable artifact headlessly. There is no vector to raster tool in the connector, so nothing in the spec asks for one: the board carries pre vectorize raster plates, the catalogue footer carries the cropped raster plate from the letterhead route, and the dark ground test for the small cut happens as inline SVG on a dark panel inside the Express specification page, read back through the rendition preview. Fonts: font_recommend, font_styles, find_fonts and get_fontkit_embed_url are the cleanest verified chain in the connector, the kit is not domain locked, and it survives into Express as the only permitted external stylesheet. font_recommend is called once per role because it refuses to pair. Typography exists only on the Express surface, never on the InDesign surface, and the spec never asks it to. InDesign: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous. The template is supplied as a client asset in the correct form, a genuine designer exported font embedding print PDF containing a placed image, which is the shape that converts, rather than a thin synthetic PDF which is verified to fail opaquely. The asset note states explicitly that the footer mark is a PLACED RASTER LOGO rather than vector artwork, which is what makes convert_pdf_to_indd yield a graphics frame with an imageHref and an integer page item id, and therefore what makes the footer swap a legal image_mappings row with action replace_all (legitimate for images, unlike for text) driven by a constant at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to the exact bare filename, all verified working in that exact shape. The mandatory IDML round trip to reconstruct true story text from Content runs is performed at step 11 and re-verified after prepare at step 16, as the documentation requires, and no loop is built on skipping it. Delivery branches are pinned to what was actually verified, and the two verified routes are not conflated: one record per page for application/pdf is verified, and createSeparateFiles on a merged x-indesign document is verified to produce one page PDFs in correct CSV order, so the eight per build sheets are PDFs from that branch with no DPI claim attached, since DPI is meaningless on a PDF and multi record raster output is verified to come back reversed with lying labels. True 300 DPI through document_render_layout is used only where it is verified, on the single record proofs, which is exactly where the print scale defects are found. Express: mixed canvas sizes in one export is verified, exact millimetre canvases resolving at 96 dpi is verified, real tables, inline SVG as native editable vector, base64 data URI images and per root data-canvas sizing are all verified, canvasWidth and canvasHeight are correctly never passed as tool params, and the readiness skill is run before the export and before the retry. One extrapolation is named rather than claimed: the largest canvas ever verified through the importer is 297 by 420 millimetres resolving to 1123 by 1587 pixels, so both large format pieces are authored as declared half scale artboards, the window at 350 by 500 millimetres and the A2 at 210 by 297 millimetres, which puts the poster exactly on a verified size and the window one modest step beyond it rather than five times past it. That single step beyond the verified envelope is stated as a run risk with a stated fallback, exporting the window panel as its own single root document if the oversized root is rejected or flattens the mixed size set. Payload is planned rather than discovered: every plate is downsampled to no more than the pixels it occupies on its destination canvas before base64 encoding, with the tradeoffs array read to confirm the operation is downward only, and the whole document is routed through the asset upload and an Adobe hosted url because seven roots of inlined photography sit far past the 70KB inline threshold. Stock and Boards: asset_search on StockAsset with a short query is verified, the broken orientation filter is never passed, isGenTech and true width and height are read, asset_license_and_download_stock at genuine camera scale is verified, and boards_create_new_board plus boards_add_items_to_board are verified headless with the twelve placement cap respected at ten in the first call and single additions afterwards, using presigned URLs rather than raw blobs, with vector correctly never sent to a board. Nothing here uses text to image, generative fill, AI object removal, background replace by prompt, cartoonize, OCR, PDF text editing, image to PDF, photo compositing or object removal. image_generative_expand, the one sanctioned generative exception, is not used at all. No video or audio tool is touched, since the entire family returns only a taskId and the named poll tools do not exist in this host. Neither fill_text, animate_design, create_firefly_board, search_design, replace_image nor download_design appears anywhere, since none yields a retrievable or trustworthy artifact here, and the consequence of download_design's absence is stated to the client as a workflow fact rather than hidden. No upscaling occurs: every source is declared at camera scale, the only resize operations are downward, image_crop_to_bounds cannot upscale and is checked instead on metadata.detection_confidence, image_crop_and_resize is checked on metadata.upscale_factor and the tradeoffs array with any upscaled entry rejected, and image_remove_background and image_fill_area are checked for a downscaled entry with the actual output dimensions recorded, since the window panel's stated effective resolution at printed size depends on it. Batch sizes stay inside limits throughout: ten frames is the multi image cap exactly, eight merge records, eleven board placements across two calls, fourteen supplied files.
human_difficulty: A skilled human freelancer would find this hard for reasons that have nothing to do with tool fluency. The engagement spans three applications with incompatible assumptions, and almost every early decision is correct on the evidence available at the time and wrong on evidence that does not exist yet. The grade that holds the specular on the polished stainless is the right grade, and it is also the reason a selection tool later cannot separate that tube from the wall behind it. The white point that splits the difference on the split light frame is the reasonable compromise, and it is also the one choice that leaves that frame matching nothing once the set is assembled. The crop rule that pads each bike by its own proportions is faithful, defensible, and produces eight bicycles at eight different sizes in an identical frame. None of those are mistakes a careless person makes; they are mistakes a careful person makes, and each of them is only visible in a condition that has to be deliberately created. The mark recovery is a genuine judgement between two bad sources, one carrying the flourish but painted on timber and shot off axis in two colours that will not survive being flattened, the other clean but nine hundred pixels and plain, and the correct answer is that both are needed at different sizes, which most people only discover at the printer. Reverse engineering a live merge template out of a flat PDF is real production work that many competent designers have never had to do, and its failure mode is a document that reports success at every stage: the reported story text is lossy, the validator passes wrong offsets without a warning, and even doing the mandatory round trip correctly proves only that a placeholder exists, not what face it will print in. Then the client's own copy, written by three people over two years, overruns a layout built around somebody else's specimen text, and the only lever available is editorial rather than mechanical. Cutting a bicycle out is notoriously the worst case for any isolation workflow, because the object is mostly holes and the defect is invisible against its original background. Sourcing the one photograph the client cannot shoot is a positioning decision disguised as a search, where the wrong pick reprices the brand faster than any typographic error. And sitting on top of all of it is the consistency problem, which is the part experienced people actually respect: eight bicycles across two lighting conditions holding one white point, one black point and one subject scale well enough to survive sitting adjacent on a page, plus a mark that is recognisably the same mark at fourteen millimetres and at a metre, plus one type system across seven canvases. That is a discipline problem rather than a technique problem, because every individual frame, page and canvas can be made to look good on its own while the set falls apart. Finally the whole thing has to be delivered in a state where one non designer with an Express seat can export the window graphic to a sign maker and reprint the catalogue next season against new numbers, which means the real deliverable is a working system rather than a set of files, and building a system takes longer than building the files and looks identical when it is finished.

engagement_title: Saltmoor Bathhouse: Cold Season rollout and Falmouth opening, from a four-lighting shoot and a photograph of a painted sign
vertical: Health, Wellness & Hospitality (independent sauna and cold-plunge bathhouse, coastal UK, two locations)
client_one_liner: Make our four-different-lighting bathhouse photographs and our six practitioner portraits look like one house, get our lost monogram back off a photograph of the painted sign, lift the retail range off the shelf shot, and prove all of it on the poster, price list, social set and practitioner cards for the Falmouth opening.
client_brief:
Saltmoor Bathhouse has run a twelve-room sauna and cold-plunge house on the seafront in Margate for three years. In November we open our second house in Falmouth, and at the same time we launch our winter programme, Cold Season, across both.

We need one visual rollout that covers both houses, and the honest problem is our photography. We shot the Margate rooms over a single day and the light fought us the whole way. The steam room is two tungsten lamps burning through steam. The plunge courtyard is open shade and goes blue. The treatment room is candles. The changing hall has a window at one end, lamps at the other, and sage-painted plaster walls throwing green into everything in between. The six practitioner portraits are worse, because three were shot by the changing-hall window and three under the changing-hall lamps on a different day entirely. Put the set side by side and it looks like four different businesses. We need it to look like one house: warm-neutral, calm, unhurried, with the water and the metalwork keeping their own colour, and nothing burnt out on the candle glass or the wet stone.

You should know that everything we have is indoors. Falmouth is a building site until the end of October so there are no pictures of it at all, and we never got outside in Margate either. The courtyard is walled, so even that frame stops at the wall.

We also need the retail range lifted off the shelf photograph, so a product can sit on a clean ground wherever we place it rather than on a shelf.

There is one more thing, and it is the piece we are most anxious about. The monogram on the painted enamel sign outside the Margate house is the only surviving version of our mark. The designer who drew it closed her studio and the working files went with her hard drive. All we have is a photograph of the sign on the wall, taken on a phone. We need that mark back as proper artwork, good enough for everywhere we use it now and everywhere we are about to.

The pieces we need:
- a campaign poster for both windows, A3
- a treatment and price list, A4, with the ritual list set as a proper table and the retail range shown on it
- a launch social set: a square post, a portrait post and a vertical story
- practitioner cards for the new house, one per practitioner, each carrying their own portrait and their own treatments, printed from the same card artwork our printer used last year. We have the print file they sent us, not the working file, and nobody here knows how it was built.
- a season reference set our two house managers can both look at, so Margate and Falmouth brief photographers and staff from the same place rather than from a folder each

Everything you hand back needs to stay editable by our small team afterwards. Please include a short written note covering what you did to the pictures, which typefaces you chose and why, and anything we should know about using the mark.

On tone: a weekday soak is 38 pounds, the Salt and Steam ritual is 72, a six-visit season pass is 195. Our people are 28 to 50, they either live locally or come down for a weekend, and they are spending carefully and deliberately. It should feel considered and generous. Not exclusive, and definitely not cheap.
price_band_and_audience:
Weekday soak 38 pounds, weekend soak 46, Salt and Steam ritual 72 (90 minutes), six-visit season pass 195, monthly membership 89. Retail: bath salt 18, botanical face oil 26, body oil 22, clay bar 14. Audience is 28 to 50, coastal-town professionals and weekenders, deliberate rather than lavish spenders.

This band is load-bearing on the design. At 38 to 72 pounds the work has to read approachable-premium: a matte warm-neutral ground for the price list and the social set, generous held space, photography that looks like a real room on a real morning rather than a rendered spa, faces present rather than removed, and prices set at body size inside the run of text rather than exiled to a quiet column. The failure at this band is a COMBINATION, not any single dark surface: near-black ground plus severe sparseness plus prices pushed out of the reading line plus people removed from the imagery is the 250-pound destination-spa answer, and it reads exclusionary here, which the client has said explicitly it must not. A saturated brand-colour panel is a different thing from a near-black one: the deep iron-blue lifted off the enamel sign is the brand's own colour and carrying the mark reversed out of it is correct at this band, provided the price list and the social set stay on the warm-neutral ground and the prices stay in the text. Drop the same content to a 12-pound municipal leisure centre and it inverts the other way (bright, busy, price set large as the headline). An agent that ships either extreme has misread the brief even if every technical gate passes.
