adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging (grading, masking, isolation, vector recovery, the one sanctioned outpaint)
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the engagement lives here and it is the surface the whole job is judged on. It levels the rolled courtyard frame, runs auto-tone as a floor, and then brings four room illuminants and a two-day portrait set to one house target with a SEPARATE adjustments call per frame, because a batched call applies one identical parameter set and that is exactly what four illuminants make wrong. It fixes the changing hall's green by selecting the sage-painted plaster surface and confining the move to that mask rather than desaturating globally. It isolates the retail range per product from tight crops, discovers that one of the four cannot be knocked to alpha at all and routes it as a solid plate instead. It recovers the monogram at ink level off a photographed painted surface, twice, from two different raster preparations. It runs the single sanctioned generative call to widen the courtyard master, then has to bring the synthesised band into the house grade before it can be used. image_vectorize sits in this family too; the real Illustrator tools are deliberately not called because their output is unretrievable headlessly.

The type system for the whole rollout. One font_recommend pass per typographic role rather than a pairing request, because the tool refuses to pair and the pairing is therefore entirely the agent's art direction against the price band. Numeric OpenType weights read from font_styles rather than assumed, every name laundered through find_fonts into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the entire kit including the valid faces beside it, and a single get_fontkit_embed_url kit whose returned CSS slugs, never the PostScript names, are what the authored HTML actually references.

Reverse-engineers the printer's flat 2024 card PDF into a live merge template, discovers on the first merged proof that two of its six fields silently never landed, repairs the mapping against the document's true story text, and then runs six practitioner cards at one record per page with per-row portraits and a per-row mark binding. Delivered as a six-page print PDF, six per-record single-page files from a route whose record identity is guaranteed, and six 300 DPI proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time.

The designed collateral as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes: A3 poster with the iron-blue brand panel and the reversed mark, A4 price list with the ritual list as a real editable table, and three social canvases that each consume a different upstream artifact. Also the mark specification page, which is the only headless route to a raster of a vector cut, and the handover page. Photographs base64-inlined because a URL renders as an empty grey box at HTTP success, the mark inlined as live SVG so it stays editable vector, the font kit embedded verbatim, and the whole document uploaded and passed by url because the payload is far past the inline threshold.

Sources and licenses the wide open-daylight winter coastal frame that the campaign turns out to need and the client does not have, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded. It is also the moment the house grade is proved wrong, because the 240px search thumbnail carries no usable colour information and the frame's real illuminant is only visible once it is licensed and downloaded.

Persists the season reference set as a real shareable board for the two house managers: the eleven final graded masters, the three mark plates and the mark specification rendition, placed inside the twelve-per-call cap with a partial-success response read as partial rather than as done.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging (Creative Cloud asset pipeline)
trajectory.action: Upload every supplied file headlessly through asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT and asset_finalize_file_upload, then actually look at each frame with asset_inline_preview before deciding anything, and write a light audit naming each frame's illuminant, its cast, its exposure error, whether it is level, and what it does and does not contain.
trajectory.reasoning: The whole engagement turns on a single house target chosen against the full set, and that target cannot be chosen from filenames. Looking first also surfaces three facts that reorder everything downstream: the courtyard frame carries a roll, the six portraits are two colour worlds rather than one, and every single frame the client owns is an interior. The last of those looks like a note and is actually the shape of the job.
trajectory.produces: Presigned URIs for all fifteen supplied assets, plus a written per-frame light audit

trajectory.action: Straighten the rolled courtyard frame with image_auto_straighten. Run image_apply_auto_tone as a floor across the set in two batched calls. Then set ONE house target by eye (warm-neutral white point, lifted but not milky black point) and reach it with a SEPARATE image_apply_adjustments call per frame, pulling highlights before lifting exposure on the three frames carrying at-risk speculars. Fix the changing hall's green by selecting the sage-painted plaster surface with image_select_by_prompt and confining an hslSaturation move to that mask.
trajectory.reasoning: Auto-tone is the only pass where batching is legitimate, because it is genuinely the same operation on every frame. The house grade is not: one imageURIs array carries one parameter set, so batching it applies identical offsets to a tungsten steam room and an open-shade courtyard and guarantees the four-different-businesses failure survives. Pulling highlights before lifting exposure is the order that saves the candle glass, the oil bottle and the wet stone; reversed, they clip and nothing downstream recovers them. And the green is a painted surface, not a hue: a global desaturation takes the cedar and the skin with it and quietly kills the warmth the whole brand is built on.
trajectory.produces: graded_house_set_v1 (four room interiors and six portraits to one target), plus the reported parameters per frame

trajectory.action: Recover the monogram off the enamel sign photograph: auto-straighten the roll, select at ink level by naming the paint's own colour and line quality rather than the sign it sits on, invert for polarity, crop to the returned bbox, fill_area the inverted mask to make a colour plate, vectorize, then strip the opaque full-canvas path at index zero and inject a viewBox by hand.
trajectory.reasoning: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the sign panel and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle that vectorizes perfectly and is worthless. Vectorizing at the wrong polarity produces a black box that also reports success. And the raw vector output ships with no viewBox and an opaque backing rectangle, neither of which any tool in the chain fixes, so the mark will not scale in an authored layout and will show as a pale box the moment it sits on colour. All three are hygiene the agent has to know to do, and none of them is a discovery.
trajectory.produces: monogram_primary.svg (full-colour, viewBox injected, backing path removed) plus the cropped ink-plate PNG

trajectory.action: Template archaeology on the printer's flat card PDF: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, and inventory what actually came back. Confirm the two graphic frames exist and read the portrait frame's bounds. Then call generate_indd_mapping_prompt, build the five text mappings and the image mapping from its reported textContent offsets, validate, and run prepare_indd_merge_template.
trajectory.reasoning: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under the agent's control, so the frame inventory has to be read rather than assumed, and the portrait frame's aspect has to be read now because the delivered portraits are 2:3 and will fill a differently proportioned frame at the wrong crop. The mapping itself is built the way the tools invite: the validator returns valid, prepare reports completed successfully, and every signal available at this point says the template is finished.
trajectory.produces: practitioner_card_template_v1.indd, reportedly carrying six live fields

trajectory.action: Clean the roster CSV (drop the duplicated row, normalise the mixed-case and trailing-space headers, reconcile the two spellings of each treatment name, reconcile the photo column's filenames against the portraits as actually delivered, add a second image column carrying the mark filename on every row). Subject-aware crop the six graded portraits to the portrait frame's aspect, reading the tradeoffs array. Round-trip the portraits and the mark PNG back through Creative Cloud storage so they carry at.adobe.com presigned URLs. Merge one record per page, render a proof, and LOOK at that proof at actual size.
trajectory.reasoning: The image column binds by exact filename, so the mismatch between the CSV's photo values and the delivered portraits is a real break to fix rather than a typo to ignore, and the duplicated row would otherwise ship a seventh card for a practitioner who does not exist. The graded portraits also live on photoshop-api.adobe.io, which is not where the merge tool will accept them from, so the round-trip is mandatory and silent if skipped. Then the proof gets inspected, because a merged page is the first artifact in this engagement where the template's real contents become visible.
trajectory.produces: card_proof_v1 (six pages, screen scale) plus an inspection finding: two of the six fields are simply not there, and the mark on the small dark panel is mush

trajectory.action: Return to the template. Download and unzip the IDML from step 4, reconstruct each frame's TRUE story text by concatenating every Content run in the Stories XML, recompute every replace_text offset against that string, re-prepare the merge template, then export IDML again and grep for all six expected placeholders before believing anything.
trajectory.reasoning: The mapping tool's reported text content is lossy: it drops a run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset after the omission is silently wrong by exactly the length of the dropped run. The validator passed it, prepare reported success, and only the merged page showed that the treatment line and the contact line never existed. Nothing available before that page could have said so, and the re-export is the only way to know the repair took.
trajectory.produces: practitioner_card_template_v2.indd with all six placeholders verified present in the round-tripped IDML

trajectory.action: Return to the mark. Re-prepare the raster as a BINARY INK MASK rather than a colour plate, vectorize that, strip the backing path, inject a viewBox, reduce to a single fill, and derive a reversed cut for dark grounds from the same preparation. Then state, by eye and honestly, the smallest size at which each of the three cuts holds.
trajectory.reasoning: The primary is built from a colour plate and comes back as dozens of near-identical fills; at poster scale that is a faithful, usable mark and at the nine millimetres it occupies on the card its fine interior strokes fill in and close up. That is not a defect in the file and it is not something a viewBox fixes. It is a scale-dependent limit that only exists once the mark has been seen at actual print size, and the answer is a genuinely different artefact built from a different raster preparation, not a cleanup of the first one. The reversed cut falls out of the same preparation and is what the card's iron-blue panel and the poster's iron-blue ground both need.
trajectory.produces: monogram_system (primary, single-colour small-size, reversed) with stated minimum usable sizes, plus the two additional ink-plate PNGs

trajectory.action: Cascade, not a discovery: re-merge against the repaired template and the single-colour mark PNG, re-render the proof, and confirm at actual size that all six fields are populated on all six cards and that the mark now reads on the iron-blue panel.
trajectory.reasoning: Two upstream artifacts the proof depended on have both changed, so the proof is not a reprint, it is a different set of pages. Re-running without re-inspecting would be the same error as merging without inspecting, one round later.
trajectory.produces: card_proof_v2 (six pages, six fields, legible mark)

trajectory.action: Run font_recommend once for the display role and once for the text role, read the numeric OpenType weight for each chosen style from font_styles, launder every name through find_fonts into canonical PostScript form, and build one embed kit for the whole rollout.
trajectory.reasoning: The tool refuses to pair, so the pairing is entirely art direction and it has to answer the price band: at 38 to 72 pounds a warm humanist text face with a quiet display companion reads considered, while a high-contrast neoclassical display overshoots into destination-spa territory the client explicitly ruled out. The numeric weights are non-standard per family, so the reflexive 400 ships Light on some families with no warning, and the CSS slug is never the PostScript name, so writing the PostScript name into the CSS ships a silent fallback. One unlaundered name in the kit call kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: type_system (display and text roles with real numeric weights and foundry credits) plus the embed kit CSS

trajectory.action: Isolate the retail range. For each of the four products separately: image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_crop_to_bounds with one to two percent padding, then image_remove_background for a transparent RGBA cutout. Record the downscale tradeoff each removal reports.
trajectory.reasoning: The shelf frame holds four separate objects with gaps between them, and background removal wants one coherent blob, so running it on the whole scene returns one product, a partial, or a merged blob and reports success either way. Tight-cropping per product first is the only route that works. Background removal also silently downscales an oversized input and says so only in a tradeoffs entry, which has to reach the resolution ledger.
trajectory.produces: retail_cutout_set_v1 (four transparent RGBA PNGs)

trajectory.action: Author the campaign as one self-contained multi-root HTML with the A3 poster PINNED AS ROOT 1: iron-blue brand ground with the reversed mark, and a three-up hero strip. Then the A4 price list on the warm-neutral ground with the ritual list as a real table and the retail cutouts on a strip. Then three social canvases: square carrying the retail range, 1080x1350 carrying one graded portrait as a practitioner-led launch card, 1080x1920 held for the story. Kit embedded verbatim with family and weight set on every text element, photographs base64-inlined, the mark inlined as SVG markup in a wrapper with explicit left, top, width and height. Upload the HTML and pass it by url. Readiness check, then export as a distinctly named document.
trajectory.reasoning: The poster goes first because the rendition preview only ever returns the first artboard, so any canvas whose defect is a colour judgement rather than a markup fact has to be root one or it cannot be looked at. Photographs referenced by URL come back as empty grey boxes at HTTP success, so the download-and-inline discipline is mandatory and invisible if skipped, and the payload with six canvases of inlined photography is far past the inline threshold, which is why the document goes up as a file and comes in by url. Setting the ritual list as a real table rather than spaced text is what keeps it editable for the client's team afterwards, which is the thing they actually asked for.
trajectory.produces: season_campaign_express_v1 plus its source HTML

trajectory.action: Verify the export properly: resolve the document's rendition through asset_search and asset_get_presigned_urls, look at root 1, and read the returned normalised markup for every root. Check fonts resolved rather than fell back, images present rather than placeholding, table structure intact, mark geometry on canvas.
trajectory.reasoning: Every one of the importer's drops returns success with no warning, so success is not fidelity and the only honest gate is to look. Two expensive things surface here, and neither of them is a markup fault. On the price list strip the amber oil bottle has come back as a solid amber disc with its enclosed neck ring filled in and its printed label collapsed, which was invisible while it sat as a transparent PNG on nothing. And on the poster, the three-up strip is three tungsten and candle interiors and the campaign is called Cold Season: there is no outside in it, no weather, no water beyond a walled courtyard, and nothing that says two houses on a coast in winter.
trajectory.produces: defect_report_v1 (one isolation defect, one campaign-level gap)

trajectory.action: Return to the isolation stage for one product only. Accept that the amber bottle cannot be knocked to alpha at all, and re-route it: select the bottle positively, invert, fill_area on the ORIGINAL frame to composite it onto a white studio ground, crop to bounds. Then change the price list's retail strip to a white band so all four products sit on one consistent ground, and write the reason into the handover.
trajectory.reasoning: Background removal cannot punch an enclosed interior; it returns the captured background as opaque pixels inside the ring, and there is no tool in the family that composites a selection mask into an alpha channel, so no amount of select-then-invert produces transparency here. The craft is recognising that one of four is a different job with a different achievable answer, and then taking the layout consequence honestly: giving the whole retail strip a white band so the plate composites invisibly, rather than shipping an amber disc onto a warm-neutral ground and hoping. That is a tool limit changing an art-direction decision, which is exactly the kind of thing that has to be documented for a team that keeps editing afterwards.
trajectory.produces: retail_isolation_set_v2 (three transparent RGBA cutouts plus one white-ground studio plate) and a revised price-list strip decision

trajectory.action: Search StockAsset with a short generic query and no orientation filter, read isGenTech to exclude generative candidates, choose on shooting height, weather and time of day rather than subject alone, license and download the wide winter coastal frame at full resolution, and look at it properly for the first time.
trajectory.reasoning: The client never asked for a bought-in picture and does not have one to give; the gap only became a fact when the poster was composed and the campaign turned out to contain no exterior. Licensed Stock is the only IP-clean route to camera-scale photography here, and the selection matters as much as the grading because the frame has to sit beside the client's own pictures without anyone spotting the join. It is also the first moment the frame's real colour is knowable: the search result carries only a 240 pixel thumbnail, which shows subject and composition and tells you nothing usable about illuminant.
trajectory.produces: licensed_coastal_master (camera scale, IP-clean, generative excluded)

trajectory.action: Return to the grade. Re-set the house neutral by eye against the full eleven-frame set now that an open-daylight reference exists in it, and re-apply the revised target as a FRESH per-frame grade computed from the ORIGINAL sources, not as a correction layered onto the v1 outputs. All eleven frames, the six portraits included.
trajectory.reasoning: The v1 target was chosen honestly and it was chosen against a set that contained two tungsten interiors, one candle interior, one mixed-illuminant interior and one open-shade courtyard, and no open-daylight reference of any kind. A target set against that set is provably wrong for any daylight frame, whatever the daylight frame turns out to be. Correcting only the licensed frame would drag it toward a neutral the rest of the set should never have had, so the honest fix is upstream, and it invalidates every graded output already consumed downstream. Grading the already-graded v1 outputs a second time would compound the original error rather than replace it.
trajectory.produces: graded_house_set_v2 (eleven frames to one revised target, licensed frame included)

trajectory.action: Build the vertical story master: image_generative_expand on the short axis of the v2 courtyard master with a fixed seed, then crop toward 9:16 and read the tradeoffs array to confirm no pixel was interpolated upward. Then look at the result.
trajectory.reasoning: A nine-by-sixteen window on the courtyard master either cuts the plunge pool in half or loses the figure, so widening first is the one sanctioned generative move available and the fixed seed is what makes the result reproducible for the client's team. Reading the tradeoff report is the only signal separating a legitimate crop from a silently upscaled one, since the crop tool will interpolate up to a two-times cap and report success either way.
trajectory.produces: story_master_expanded (wider canvas, seed recorded)

trajectory.action: Return to the grade for this one frame. The expanded band is new pixels that were synthesised from the source and never passed through the house grade, so bring the expanded master back to the house neutral with its own adjustments pass before cropping, then crop to 1080x1920. Only then apply the story's stylized treatment: select the water surface, invert, and tint everything except the water to the iron-blue.
trajectory.reasoning: Generative expand builds its new edge content from the frame it is given and does not carry a colour target forward; the added sky and stone come back sitting outside the house neutral, and the seam is visible precisely where the eye goes on a full-screen canvas. The order matters too: regrade, then crop, then tint. Tinting before the regrade would bake the mismatch in under the treatment, and cropping before the regrade would just make the mismatched band harder to see while leaving it in the file.
trajectory.produces: story_master_9x16 (regraded, cropped, water-masked tint applied, no output pixel above source scale)

trajectory.action: Cascade, not a discovery: re-run the card merge against the v2 portraits and the single-colour mark, re-cropped to the portrait frame's aspect and re-uploaded to Creative Cloud storage, then deliver three ways. One six-page print PDF. Six per-record single-page files, produced by merging to InDesign format and rendering with createSeparateFiles so record identity is guaranteed. Six proofs rendered at 300 DPI from the merged document.
trajectory.reasoning: The proof run was built from portraits and a mark that have both since been superseded, so the pages are fine and their contents are stale. The per-record files have to come from a route whose record identity is guaranteed rather than from multi-record raster output, whose returned order is reversed relative to its own labels, so naming by position in the returned list ships the wrong practitioner on the wrong card, confidently. And the high-resolution proofs have to be rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time, because the merge step ignores the resolution field and hands back screen-scale pages while reporting success.
trajectory.produces: practitioner_card_run (six-page print PDF, six named per-record PDFs, six 300 DPI proofs)

trajectory.action: Cascade, not a discovery: re-author the campaign HTML with the v2 photography re-downloaded and re-inlined, the licensed frame in the poster's hero strip, the amber plate and the white retail band on the price list, the expanded story master in the vertical root, and the three mark cuts placed by context (primary large, single-colour small, reversed on the iron-blue). Readiness check, export under a distinct v2 name.
trajectory.reasoning: Base64 payloads are baked into the document, so a regrade upstream means every photograph in the file is stale until it is re-downloaded and re-inlined; there is no relink and no partial update. Placing the right mark cut per context is the entire point of having built three, and using the primary everywhere is exactly the decision a non-designer makes. The distinct document name matters because every export mints a new document and the verification search has to resolve one thing rather than three near-identical ones.
trajectory.produces: season_campaign_express_v2

trajectory.action: Verify the re-export the same way: rendition preview for root 1, returned markup for every root, and a specific check that the three-up strip now reads as one set and that the price list's retail band carries four products on one ground.
trajectory.reasoning: The point of a self-correcting loop is that it closes. Re-exporting without re-inspecting is the same error as exporting without inspecting, and both of the defects this pass is checking were invisible until something was rendered and looked at.
trajectory.produces: verification_pass_2

trajectory.action: Author a single-root mark specification page carrying all three cuts inline as SVG with their minimum sizes, export it as its own small document, then resolve its rendition through asset_search and asset_get_presigned_urls.
trajectory.reasoning: Nothing in the toolchain rasterises an SVG, and the board will not take vector, so the only headless route to a picture of a vector cut is to put the cuts on a canvas and resolve that canvas's rendition. All three cuts have to sit on ONE root, because the rendition returns the first artboard only and a three-page specification would come back as one page. It costs one extra export and it is the difference between a reference the house managers can actually see and a promise.
trajectory.produces: mark_specification_page (Express doc) plus its resolved rendition raster

trajectory.action: Create the season reference board and populate it with the eleven v2 masters, the three mark plates and the mark specification rendition: fifteen items across two calls of twelve and three, every item re-uploaded through Creative Cloud storage first so the URLs are on the domain the board tool takes, and a 201 read as partial success with only the entries listed as failed re-sent.
trajectory.reasoning: Two house managers briefing from two folders is how the four-different-businesses problem returns next season, so the reference has to be one persisted shareable thing rather than a zip. The per-call cap is hard, vector is not placeable, and a partial-success response looks exactly like a success unless it is read, which is why the item count gets verified rather than assumed.
trajectory.produces: season_reference_board (live shareable board, fifteen items verified, zero failed placements)

trajectory.action: Add the handover and specification root to the campaign document and export a final time: the grade parameters applied per frame and why, the type roles with their real numeric weights and foundry credits, the three mark cuts with their minimum usable sizes and where each belongs, the retail isolation inventory including which product could not be delivered transparent and why the strip is white because of it, the expand seed, the resolution ledger showing every output against its source, and the reference board link.
trajectory.reasoning: This page can only be written once every parameter is settled, which is why it comes last and costs one more export rather than being drafted early with blanks. It is also the deliverable that makes everything else maintainable by a small in-house team, which is what the client actually asked for when they said everything has to stay editable, and it is where the one honest limitation in the retail set gets stated plainly instead of hidden.
trajectory.produces: season_campaign_express_final (poster, price list, three social canvases, handover root) plus handover_note

trajectory.action: Final pass across all surfaces: page count equals cleaned roster row count, all six merge fields populated on all six cards, each card carrying its own correct portrait, every canvas at its declared size, every photograph rendering rather than placeholding, fonts resolved rather than fallen back, every mark instance carrying a viewBox with no backing rectangle and the right cut for its context, board item count exact with zero failures, and no output anywhere exceeding its source resolution.
trajectory.reasoning: Every failure mode in this engagement is silent and most of them are cross-surface, so the last honest act is to check them as a set rather than trusting that each surface reported success on its own. Four of these gates were already violated once during the job and repaired; the ledger is what proves the repairs held everywhere rather than in the place they were noticed.
trajectory.produces: qa_ledger

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The first merged proof shows that two of the six fields, the treatment line and the contact line, do not exist on any card. Nothing said so before this page: the mapping tool reported a well-formed story string, the validator returned valid with zero warnings, and prepare reported completed successfully. The reported text content had silently dropped one run while keeping its line break, so the string still read as correct and every offset after the omission was wrong by exactly the length of the dropped run.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The template is rebuilt against the document's true story text: download and unzip the IDML, concatenate every Content run in the Stories XML, recompute all offsets from that string, re-prepare, then re-export IDML and confirm every one of the six placeholders is actually present before trusting it again.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: Six practitioner cards go to the printer with no treatment line and no contact details on any of them, for a new house whose whole point is that guests can find the right practitioner and book. The client discovers it on the delivered print run, and every tool response in the chain will have said the template was fine.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: At the roughly nine millimetres the monogram occupies on the card's iron-blue panel, the recovered mark closes up. It is a vectorisation built from a colour plate, so it carries dozens of near-identical fills and its fine interior strokes merge into each other at that scale. At poster size the same file is faithful and entirely usable, which is why nothing about it looked wrong until a card was proofed at actual size.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: A second cut is built from a different raster preparation: a binary ink mask rather than a colour plate, vectorised, backing path stripped, viewBox injected, reduced to a single fill. A reversed cut for dark grounds falls out of the same preparation. Each of the three cuts gets a stated minimum usable size, arrived at by looking rather than by hoping.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: Every card in the print run carries a mark that has lost its interior detail on the one panel where it has to survive at nine millimetres, and the poster's iron-blue ground has no reversed cut to sit on it, so either the mark goes on as a positive that disappears or a pale plate gets dropped behind it. The client's real question, how small can we go, is left unanswered because nothing was built that could answer it.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: On the price list strip the amber oil bottle has come back as a solid amber disc: its enclosed see-through neck ring is filled with the shelf that was behind it, and its printed paper label has collapsed. The transparent cutout looked correct on its own and the tool reported success. Background removal cannot punch an enclosed interior hole, and nothing else in the family composites a selection mask into an alpha channel, so there is no route to a transparent version of this product at all.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: That one product is re-routed as a solid plate: select the bottle positively, invert, fill onto a white studio ground on the original frame, crop to bounds. The layout then has to change with it, because a white plate on a warm-neutral panel shows as a white rectangle, so the price list's retail strip becomes a white band and all four products sit on one consistent ground. The handover states which product is different and why.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The price list ships with an opaque amber disc where a bottle should be, with the label unreadable, on the one page that carries the retail prices the client is trying to sell. It also ships a false promise in the handover, that all four products are available as transparent assets, which the client's team will act on for the next year.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The house neutral is wrong, and it was wrong from the moment it was set. The composed poster made the campaign gap visible first: three tungsten and candle interiors in the hero strip, nothing outdoors, nothing seasonal, for a programme called Cold Season across two coastal houses. Sourcing the missing wide open-daylight frame then exposes the deeper problem, which is structural rather than aesthetic. The client's five frames are two tungsten, one candle, one mixed-illuminant and one open-shade courtyard, so the set the target was chosen against contained no open-daylight reference at all. A neutral set against that set is provably wrong for any daylight frame, whichever one is licensed. The licensed frame's own illuminant could not have been read earlier either, because the search result carries only a 240 pixel thumbnail.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The shared house target is re-set by eye against the full eleven-frame set with the daylight frame in it, and then re-applied as a fresh per-frame grade computed from the original sources, six practitioner portraits included, since those are already downstream inside a merged card run. Grading the v1 outputs a second time would compound the original error instead of replacing it.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The poster ships with one obviously bought-in picture sitting in the hero strip next to the client's own rooms, and the printed practitioner cards ship in a visibly different colour world from the campaign in the window beside them. That is precisely the four-different-businesses failure the client hired the job to fix, arriving in the finished work rather than the raw files.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The expanded courtyard master does not sit at the house neutral. Generative expand builds its new edge content from the frame it is handed and carries no colour target forward, so the added sky and stone come back outside the grade, with the seam falling exactly where the eye lands on a full-screen vertical canvas. This could not have been known before the expand ran, because the pixels did not exist until it did.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The expanded master goes back through the grading stage for its own adjustments pass to bring the synthesised band to the house neutral, and only then is it cropped to 1080x1920 and given the water-masked tint. The order is load-bearing: tinting first would bake the mismatch in underneath the treatment, and cropping first would hide it without removing it.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The launch story, the one canvas that gets seen full screen and edge to edge, ships with a visible tonal seam across the sky where the real frame ends and the generated pixels begin, on a campaign whose entire premise is that the pictures finally look like one house.

deliverables.name: graded_house_set_v2
deliverables.spec: Eleven frames brought to one house look: four room interiors shot under four different illuminants, six practitioner portraits shot across two days under two light sources, and the licensed winter coastal frame. Courtyard frame levelled. The retail shelf frame is deliberately excluded and graded separately to a neutral product target, because it is a cut-out source destined for a white ground, not a room. Acceptance: one white point and one black point across the eleven when frames are placed adjacent, which is where it is judged; no frame reads warmer, cooler, greener or muddier than the set; speculars held on the candle glass, the oil bottle and the wet stone rather than clipped; the water still reads cold; the licensed frame indistinguishable in colour world from the client's own; no output above its source resolution, with any tool-reported downscale recorded.

deliverables.name: retail_isolation_set
deliverables.spec: Four retail products isolated per product from tight crops of one shelf frame, each product routed to the treatment it can actually receive. Three products (salt tin, clay bar, opaque body oil) delivered as transparent RGBA cutouts with alpha intact through every downstream crop. The amber face oil is delivered as a white-ground studio plate ONLY, because its enclosed neck ring cannot be knocked to alpha by any available route, and the layout carries that constraint: the price list's retail strip becomes a white band so all four sit on one ground. Acceptance: three genuine RGBA cutouts; one plate; the amber bottle's printed label intact and legible on the plate; the handover states plainly which product is different and why; and no naive four-way knockout shipped, which would put an opaque amber disc on a coloured ground.

deliverables.name: monogram_mark_system
deliverables.spec: The client's lost monogram recovered from a photograph of a painted enamel sign, as three real vector cuts built from two different raster preparations: a full-colour primary from a colour plate, a simplified single-colour cut from a binary ink mask for small sizes, and a reversed cut for dark grounds. Every cut carries an injected viewBox and has the opaque full-canvas backing path removed, and every cut arrives in the campaign document as live editable paths rather than a placed picture. Each cut ships with its stated minimum usable size and the context it belongs in. Acceptance: the mark reads as the mark and not as a sign-shaped rectangle; the small cut holds at the nine millimetres it occupies on the printed card; the reversed cut sits on the iron-blue ground with no pale plate behind it.

deliverables.name: practitioner_card_run
deliverables.spec: Six practitioner cards built from the printer's flat 2024 press PDF reverse-engineered into a live merge template, with per-record portraits bound from the graded set through an image column and the single-colour mark bound to the card's small mark frame. Delivered as one six-page print PDF with page count equal to the cleaned roster row count (the duplicated row removed), six per-record single-page files named to the roster and produced by a route whose record identity is guaranteed, and six proofs rendered at 300 DPI from the merged document. Trim equals media box, matching the supplied 2024 artwork: no bleed is introduced and no named press preset is applied, because a PDF-derived template carries neither. Acceptance: all six fields present and populated on all six cards, each card carrying its own correct portrait cropped to the frame's own aspect rather than squeezed into it, no card carrying a placeholder image, and no per-record file naming a practitioner it does not contain.

deliverables.name: season_campaign_express
deliverables.spec: One native editable Adobe Express document at mixed canvas sizes plus its source HTML, carrying six roots that each do different work: the A3 poster at true physical dimensions on the deep iron-blue brand ground with the reversed mark and the three-up hero strip; the A4 treatment and price list on the warm-neutral ground with the ritual list as a real editable table, prices at body size in the run of text, and the retail range on its white strip; a 1080x1080 square post carrying the retail range; a 1080x1350 portrait post carrying one graded practitioner portrait as a launch card; a 1080x1920 story built from the outpainted, regraded courtyard master with the water-masked iron-blue tint; and the handover and specification root. A separate single-root mark specification document carries the three cuts and their minimum sizes. Acceptance: every photograph renders rather than placeholding, the chosen Adobe Fonts resolve rather than falling back to the importer default, the price list is a real table, and every mark instance is editable vector. This document is the editable screen-scale deliverable; the press-resolution output in this engagement comes from the card run.

deliverables.name: season_reference_board
deliverables.spec: A persisted, shareable Adobe Board the two house managers both work from, holding the eleven final graded masters, the three mark plates and the mark specification rendition. Fifteen items placed across two calls inside the twelve-per-call cap, with the partial-success response read as partial. Acceptance: the board exists at a live URL, the item count is exactly fifteen, and there are zero failed placements. Its selection is judged as art direction: it is what Margate and Falmouth will both brief photographers and staff from next season, so what is on it and what is left off it is the deliverable.

decision_gates: Naming the substrate when selecting the monogram (the mark on the sign, the emblem on the enamel panel) pulls the selection to the sign panel and returns a rectangle; naming the graphic's own visual properties (the cream painted line monogram) returns the strokes. Both report success, and every downstream step on the wrong one produces a sign-shaped blob that vectorises perfectly.

Vectorising the recovered mask at the wrong polarity yields a rectangle with the monogram knocked out of it, which also reports success. One inversion is the entire difference between a mark and a box.

The raw vector output has no viewBox and a full-canvas opaque backing path, and nothing in the toolchain fixes either. Skip them and the mark will not scale in the authored layout and will show as a pale box the moment it sits on the poster's iron-blue ground. This is hygiene the agent has to know to perform, not something any response will flag.

Batching the house grade is the reasonable-looking shortcut that guarantees the failure. One multi-image adjustments call carries one parameter set, so it applies identical offsets to a tungsten steam room and an open-shade courtyard. Auto-tone is the only pass where batching is honest; the house grade is one call per frame.

The order of operations inside the grade is irreversible: highlights on the candle glass, the oil bottle and the wet stone must be pulled before exposure is lifted. Auto-tone alone blows them and no later step recovers a clipped specular.

The changing hall's green is a painted surface, not a hue. It needs the sage plaster selected and the move confined to that mask. A global desaturation, or a global HSL rotation on the frame, takes the cedar and the skin tones with it and quietly kills the warmth the whole brand is built on.

The house neutral has to be chosen against a set that contains an open-daylight reference. The client's five frames contain none, so a target set against them alone is structurally wrong for any daylight frame that later joins the set, whichever one it is. This is not a sequencing mistake to be avoided by planning; it is a property of the material the client owns.

The four retail products need three different answers, not one. A tight per-product crop first, because background removal wants one coherent blob and four objects on a shelf return a partial or a merge. Then transparent RGBA for the three opaque products, and the recognition that the fourth cannot be transparent at all, since an enclosed ring cannot be punched to alpha and no tool converts a selection mask into an alpha channel. Shipping the naive four-way knockout puts an opaque amber disc with a collapsed label onto the price list.

That constraint has to change the layout, not just the file. A white studio plate on a warm-neutral panel reads as a white rectangle, so the retail strip becomes a white band and all four products sit on one ground. A non-designer keeps the ground and hopes the plate blends.

Trusting the mapping tool's reported text content silently loses a run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset after the omission is wrong. The validator passes it, prepare reports success, and two of six fields simply never exist. The only route to knowing is reconstructing the true story from the IDML content runs and re-verifying the placeholders afterwards.

The portrait frame's aspect has to be read out of the exported IDML before the portraits are bound. The delivered portraits are 2:3 and the frame is not, so binding them unprepared fills the frame at whatever crop the layout engine picks rather than the one a person would choose.

Per-record files must come from a route whose record identity is guaranteed. Multi-record raster output comes back reversed relative to its own labels, so naming files by their position in the returned list ships the wrong practitioner on the wrong card, correctly and confidently.

The merge step ignores the resolution field and hands back screen-scale pages while reporting success, so 300 DPI proofs have to be rendered from the merged document afterwards. Requesting resolution at merge time is the plausible-looking call that silently ships 72 DPI to a printer.

Photographs referenced by URL in the authored HTML render as empty grey boxes at HTTP success. The download and inline step is mandatory, has to be repeated in full after any regrade because the pixels are baked into the document, and there is no relink. The poster also has to be root one, because the rendition preview returns the first artboard only and a colour judgement cannot be made from markup.

Numeric font weights are non-standard per family and the CSS family name is never the PostScript name. Writing the reflexive weight ships the wrong cut, writing the PostScript name ships a silent fallback, and one unlaundered name kills the entire embed kit including the valid faces alongside it.

Which canvas gets the stylized treatment is a taste call a non-designer gets wrong by tinting everything. The masked tint belongs on the vertical story, where the water surface is excluded so it alone stays cold, and it belongs nowhere near the practitioner portraits or the retail products.

The price band decides the layout, and the failure is a combination rather than a colour. At 38 to 72 pounds a saturated iron-blue brand panel carrying the reversed mark is correct, provided the price list and social set stay warm-neutral, prices stay at body size inside the text, and people stay in the pictures. Near-black plus severe sparseness plus prices exiled to a column plus faces removed is the 250-pound answer, and the client said explicitly it must not read that way.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a one-shot image model and everything that comes back fails on one of three counts. Identity: the client needs their actual steam room, their actual six practitioners and the actual monogram off their actual sign, and a generative model will redraw all three into plausible strangers, which is a legal and practical non-starter for a business whose named staff appear on printed cards that a printer is about to run. Specification: six roster rows must yield exactly six pages with the duplicate removed, the cards must match the printer's existing artwork the client is reordering against down to the frame the mark sits in, the canvases are A3, A4 and three fixed social sizes, the proofs are 300 DPI, the sourced frame must be licensed and provably not generative, and no output may exceed its source resolution. A regeneration hits none of those and cannot be asked to. Editability: the client's entire stated requirement is that a small in-house team keeps working on this afterwards, which means a live merge template, a real editable table, live vector mark paths and a native editable document, not a flat picture of a design. And the load-bearing craft is consistency across eleven frames shot under five illuminants across two days plus one bought-in frame, judged by adjacency, which is the one thing a per-image regeneration is structurally incapable of holding.
doability_proof:
Every step maps to a tool verified live on 2026-09-10 on an auth account, and nothing in the chain touches a banned capability.

INGEST. asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT, asset_finalize_file_upload for all fifteen supplied files. Fully headless, no file picker. asset_inline_preview lets the model actually look before choosing grade parameters, which the imaging tools require anyway. Fifteen supplied plus one licensed Stock frame is sixteen uploads; the imaging family touches thirteen of them (four rooms, one shelf, six portraits, one sign, one licensed), comfortably under the ~20 overall limit, and every multi-image call stays under the 10-per-call cap.

IMAGING. image_auto_straighten on the courtyard roll and on the sign photograph (roll only, which is all either needs; no keystone correction is asked for anywhere, because the sign is declared shot square-on). image_apply_auto_tone as an identical floor pass, and this is the ONLY place batching is used: two calls of at most ten. The house grade is ONE image_apply_adjustments call PER FRAME, eleven calls, because imageURIs carries a single parameter set and batching it would apply identical offsets across four illuminants. Frames carrying at-risk speculars get two sequential calls so highlights are pulled before exposure is lifted, which cannot be expressed inside one call. The changing hall's green is fixed via image_select_by_prompt on the sage-painted plaster surface (material and texture selection is verified: a painted plank surface returned a clean 672,398 px mask) then image_apply_adjustments with that maskURI, which is the verified route; image_adjust_single_color_saturation is the surfaced alternative if a mask proves unnecessary. A global hslSaturation move without a mask is explicitly the failure the gates name.

ISOLATION. Per product: image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox true, image_crop_to_bounds with 1 to 2 percent padding, then image_remove_background on that tight crop for transparent RGBA, since removal is strictly single-image, whole-frame, and needs one coherent blob (four objects on a shelf collapse or partial). The tradeoffs array is read for the silent downscale on oversized input. The amber bottle is NOT specced transparent anywhere: image_remove_background is confirmed unable to punch an enclosed interior (it returned a solid opaque disc, 118,823 opaque px where ~18,000 was correct), selection masks carry alpha uniformly 255, and no tool composites a maskURI into an alpha channel. It is routed instead through image_select_by_prompt, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area on the ORIGINAL with preset "white" and opacity 100 (the verified white-knockout-plate variant), then image_crop_to_bounds. Alpha survives both crop tools at outputFileType png, verified, and png is held through the whole chain.

THE SINGLE GENERATIVE CALL. image_generative_expand on the courtyard master's short axis with a fixed seed, then a per-frame image_apply_adjustments pass on the expanded result, then image_crop_and_resize to 1080x1920. No upscaling anywhere: sources are declared at camera scale (4480x2987 rooms and shelf, 3648x5472 portraits, 3024x4032 sign, licensed Stock at camera scale around 7360x4912), every destination canvas is smaller (A3 1123x1587, A4 794x1123, social at most 1080x1920, card portrait frame around 1000x1400 at 300 DPI, mark frame around 106 px at nine millimetres), and the agent reads metadata.upscale_factor and the tradeoffs array to confirm rather than assert it. The crop tool's two-times cap is never approached.

VECTOR RECOVERY. image_select_by_prompt at ink level, image_invert_selection for polarity, image_crop_to_bounds, image_vectorize, then local viewBox injection and removal of path index zero. Twice, from two different raster preparations: a fill_area colour plate for the primary and a binary mask for the single-colour and reversed cuts, since image_vectorize takes no options at all and the raster prep is the only lever. Illustrator's own tools (document_render_vector, document_merge_data_vector) are deliberately not called, because both sit on the dead vectorPollingHelper path and are unretrievable headlessly.

TYPOGRAPHY. font_recommend once per role, font_styles for the numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder every name, get_fontkit_embed_url once for the whole system, kit CSS pasted verbatim as the only external stylesheet, families[].css_stack slug used as the family and the numeric weight set on every text element.

LAYOUT AND MERGE. The merge template is SUPPLIED as a client asset, the printer's real font-embedding press PDF from a genuine page layout, exactly as the mandate requires. convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml to inventory frames and read the portrait frame's bounds (a source PDF with two placed images is verified to expose two graphic frames usable as image_mappings targets, which is why the asset note declares two), generate_indd_mapping_prompt, then the mandatory IDML round-trip to reconstruct true story offsets, prepare_indd_merge_template with the whole mapping passed as a JSON string in params.mappingJson, then export_idml again to grep every placeholder. Merge inputs must live on the right host: the graded portraits and the mark PNG come off photoshop-api.adobe.io, so each is curl -L'd and re-uploaded through asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, and THOSE presigned URLs go into additionalImageFiles with keys matching the bare filenames in the @-prefixed CSV columns exactly. Two image columns: @photo per row, and @mark carrying the same filename on every row, which is the verified per-row binding shape and the only route to putting the mark in that frame. document_merge_data_layout at one record per page for the print PDF; merge to application/x-indesign then document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles true for the per-record files in guaranteed order; document_render_layout with resolution 300 for the proofs, because outputSpecs.resolution is silently ignored at merge time. No variable QR (never produced), no bleed gate (a PDF-derived template carries none and the deliverable says so), no pdfPreset (closed undiscoverable enum, 422s on every value), no N-up, and no text action replace_all.

AUTHORING. create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill before EVERY export and every retry, export_html_to_express with mixed canvas sizes in one document via per-root data-canvas attributes and no global canvasWidth/canvasHeight/slideSelector overrides. Photographs base64-inlined as data URIs on img tags, never URL-referenced and never as CSS background-image. The mark inlined as SVG markup (about 25 percent smaller than a base64 data URI and the form the readiness skill prefers) inside wrappers carrying explicit left, top, width and height. TRANSPORT: six roots of inlined photography are far past the 70 KB inline threshold, so the HTML is uploaded with media_type text/html and the returned *.adobe.com presignedAssetUrl is passed as the `url` param, which the importer accepts. Each export uses a DISTINCT docName (_v1 / _v2 / _final / _markspec) so the verification asset_search resolves one document rather than three near-identical ones, and the final name is recorded in the QA ledger. Verification via asset_search on CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview for root one (the poster, pinned first because the rendition returns page one only) plus the returned per-slide HzHTML for every other root.

STOCK AND BOARDS. asset_search with entityScope StockAsset, a short generic query and NO orientation filter (orientation returns zero hits), isGenTech read to exclude generative candidates, asset_license_and_download_stock then an immediate curl of the one-hour presigned URL. boards_create_new_board plus boards_add_items_to_board with presignedUrl items, fifteen items across two calls of twelve and three inside the hard per-call cap, HTTP 201 read as partial success with only failedItems re-sent. Board items are all raster: the eleven graded masters, the three ink-plate PNGs from the vector preparations, and the mark specification page's resolved rendition, since boards reject vector and nothing in the connector rasterises an SVG. create_firefly_board is not used because it persists nothing.

NOT USED ANYWHERE: text-to-image, generative fill, AI object removal, background-replace-by-prompt, cartoonize, upscaling, OCR, PDF text editing, image-to-PDF, photo compositing, object removal, per-artboard named export, responsive layout, replace_image, download_design, animate_design, fill_text, search_design, and video or audio of any kind. The Express deliverable is correctly specified as the editable document plus its source HTML rather than an exported file, and the press-resolution deliverable comes from the InDesign render path where 300 DPI is genuinely achievable.

FAMILY ACCOUNTING, stated deliberately rather than by default: this is filed under Photo & Image against the 30-task quota because the primary deliverables are the eleven-frame graded set, the isolation set and the recovered mark system, which is where the craft, the risk and the client's own stated anxiety all sit, and which the deliverables array leads with. The collateral surfaces are where that work is proved and are genuinely heavy, so a Layout & Data filing would also be defensible; the Photo & Image filing is chosen because the collateral is downstream of, and invalidated by, the imaging decisions rather than the other way round.
human_difficulty:
A skilled freelancer would quote this at several days and still expect to lose an evening to it. Colour-matching eleven frames shot under five illuminants across two days into one convincing house look is the hardest routine thing in commercial retouching, and it is judged by adjacency, which means the work looks finished right up until the moment three frames sit side by side on a poster. Bringing a bought-in licensed frame into that same look without it reading as bought-in is harder still, and almost nobody gets the house neutral right on the first pass here, because the correct target depends on a reference the client's own material does not contain. Discovering that the shoot has no outdoors in it at all, and that the campaign therefore has no season in it, is the kind of thing you notice when you lay out the poster and not when you read the brief.

Recovering a mark from a phone photograph of a weathered painted sign is reconstruction, not tracing: the paint has a highlight roll across it, the ground is a deep saturated colour rather than white, and the result has to hold at both poster scale and nine millimetres, which in practice means drawing two different marks from two different preparations and knowing why. Deciding the minimum size honestly, rather than in the client's favour, is a judgement a lot of designers get wrong and then regret at the printer.

The retail range looks like one job and is three. Recognising that one of four products simply cannot be delivered the way the other three can, and then changing the layout to accommodate that rather than pretending, is the kind of constraint reasoning that separates someone who knows their tools from someone who trusts them. It is also the sort of thing that goes unnoticed in the file and becomes obvious the instant the asset lands on colour.

Reverse-engineering a printer's flat press PDF into a working merge template is the job people take on assuming twenty minutes and finish four hours later, because the frame structure of the converted document is not under your control, the field boundaries are not where the visual blocks suggest, and the tooling will tell you it worked when it did not. The messy roster, with its duplicated row, its two spellings per treatment and its filenames that do not match the photographs as delivered, is exactly the client data every freelancer actually receives.

And then the whole thing has to hold as one system across four production surfaces with four different colour and typography behaviours, for a price band that punishes both directions: overshoot into luxury and it stops feeling like somewhere you would go on a Tuesday, undershoot and a 72-pound ritual looks overpriced. Holding that line while going back five separate times into work you had already called finished, twice into the grade, once into the mark, once into the cutouts and once into the merge template, is the part that makes it a real commission rather than an exercise.

engagement_title: Thornbeck Athletic AFC, 125th season: recover the 1901 crest from a scan and a pin badge, prove and separate it for the screen printer, and roll it out across the shop, the launch campaign and an 18-player kit-order run
vertical: Apparel, Merch & Sports Club Retail (English non-league football, supporter-owned)
client_one_liner: Get our old crest back as real artwork we own, separated and proofed the way our printer needs it, then use it to launch the 125th-season kit: shop images for three colourways, a poster and social set, the Boxing Day programme cover, and a kit-order card for every player in the squad.
client_brief:
Thornbeck Athletic AFC is a supporter-owned football club in West Yorkshire, fifth tier, and next season is our 125th. We are relaunching the kit and reopening the club shop for it, and we have a problem: nobody has the artwork.

The crest has been on our shirts since 1901 and the club has never owned a digital version of it. What we hold is the cover of a 1974 matchday programme that a member had scanned at the town library, a 1968 enamel pin badge photographed on somebody's kitchen worktop, and last season's supporters' tee with the crest screen-printed across the chest. The programme paper has yellowed and the printing has drifted slightly out of register. The badge photo is the truest surviving record of our oxblood and sand, but it is shot at an angle with window light bouncing off the enamel and a raised metal lip all the way round. The supporters' tee is the only place anyone can still see the aged, broken-up look our chest print has always had, and the members like it and want it kept. We need the crest recovered properly out of what exists and handed back as artwork we own and can hold at any size. The heron, the weir bars under it, the name scroll and the date ring all have to survive; the heron is the club and the members will notice if its legs go wrong.

Our printer will not take a flat picture. He needs the crest broken into the inks he lays down: up to four on the chest, plus the aged texture screened as its own pass, plus an under-white on the dark garments. He also wants a proof showing all the passes back together as one image before he burns any screens, because he has been sent separations before with a piece missing and nobody noticed until the shirts were wrong. He has asked for a version that works on the sleeve badge, which finishes at 24mm across, and on the woven neck label, which is smaller again. His note about line weights and passes is attached. Whatever you give him has to come with a written page telling him which artwork to use at which size and what each pass is, and he has to be able to open that page himself with no design software on his machine, because he will phone us if he cannot.

Alongside that, the shop and the launch. Three shirt colourways were photographed by two different volunteers on different days in a garage, and they do not look like they belong to the same shop; they need to read as one line, cut out and sitting on our shop background. Then the launch itself: a poster for the ground and the town centre, the cover of the Boxing Day programme against Aldercar Town, the page people land on from the shop link, and posts for the feed and for stories. You are choosing the type; the only wordmark file we have is a 320-pixel PNG somebody pulled off the old website years ago and it is no use to anybody for print. And nothing goes to the printer until the trust committee has seen the whole thing in one place, so we need somewhere online we can all look at it together before the vote at the next meeting.

Finally, every player has to be sized and ordered for. Our printer works from a kit-order card, one card per player, carrying their name, squad number, size and chosen colourway, and he has sent us the card he prints from. He wants the run as one file he can put straight on the press, and he also wants each player as his own separate file, because there is always a reorder in February and he does not want to be pulling one page out of eighteen. The kit office wants proofs at print quality before any of it goes anywhere. Our club secretary keeps the squad on a spreadsheet which is, honestly, a mess: four people have typed into it over two seasons. There are eighteen in the squad, and the season starts whether or not we have chased everybody, so please do not stop and wait on us. Make a sensible call, write down what you assumed, and we will confirm it.

On price and tone: the replica shirt is 58 pounds, the heavyweight supporters' tee 26 pounds, the enamel pin 8 pounds, the matchday programme 3 pounds. Our buyers are the people who own the club. Mostly 25 to 65, a lot of families, many of them buying a shirt they will still be wearing in five years. This is not a fashion drop and it is not a bargain bin. It should look like a club that has been here 125 years and knows it.

Everything you hand over has to be something our volunteers can keep working with in-house afterwards, and please write down what you did and why, especially the crest decisions and the print constraints, so we can pass it to the printer and to whoever does this next season.
price_band_and_audience: Replica shirt 58 pounds, heavyweight supporters' tee 26 pounds, enamel pin 8 pounds, matchday programme 3 pounds; audience is the club's own membership, 25 to 65, heavily family, buying a five-season garment rather than a seasonal drop. The band is load-bearing on the design: at 58 pounds for a fifth-tier replica sold to the people who own the club, the work has to read civic and archival, which means one honest spot-ink system with the recovered crest given room, quiet numerals, generous held space, and no gradient sheen, no starburst price flash, no fashion-drop cropping. A 120-pound performance-brand launch would justify a technical, high-contrast, motion-led look, and a 12-pound charity tee would justify clip-art and a loud price; both would be visibly wrong here, and the restraint is the thing the members are actually paying for. The band also decides which mark leads: the recovered historical crest carries the poster and the programme cover, and the simplified small-use mark is confined to the sizes it was built for.

adobe_surfaces.role: Ink-level selection of the crest off the yellowed 1974 scan, mask polarity handling, per-element knockout plates via masked white fill, the simplified small-use mark built by masked erasure and solid fill, the screened texture pass halftoned off the supporters' tee at a chosen radius with the lettering held crisp, auto-straighten and per-garment tonal work across the three garage shots, subject-aware crops that must not interpolate up, and both knockout treatments the two destinations turn out to need.
