adobe_surfaces.role: Converting each prepared plate raster into vector paths, and the vector hygiene and assembly the tool does not do: injecting a viewBox, deleting the opaque full-canvas path, flattening the plate union into the under-white silhouette, assigning the club's two spot colours as local fill edits, and recombining plates into the two-ink lockup. Honest note: these are Illustrator-family outputs produced through the imaging endpoint; the true Illustrator tools (document_render_vector, document_merge_data_vector) are unretrievable headlessly and are deliberately never called. Fold this entry into imaging and the task still stands at six distinct surfaces.

Choosing and licensing the two typographic roles the club never had: a display and nameset face for the crest lockup, poster and shirt-name specimen, and a text face for the collateral and the handover sheet. Supplies the real numeric weights, the correct family slugs for display cuts, and the embeddable kit that carries live type into the Express documents. Visited twice, because the only proof a face actually took comes back from the importer.

Licensed, IP-clean floodlit terrace photography at camera scale for the A3 poster ground and the 9:16 story canvas, downscaled only. It is the only legally clean source of photography the club does not already own, and it is visited twice, because a frame that holds at A3 need not survive a portrait crop when outpainting a photograph of real supporters is refused on editorial grounds.

Reverse-engineering the printer's flat A6 card PDF into a live merge template with real placeholders and two bound image frames, then producing the 18-record run: one press PDF at one card per page, eighteen per-player named single-page PDFs, and 300 dpi proofs, with the garment swatch bound per row to the agent's own cutouts and the crest bound identically on every row.

The whole launch campaign and both proof surfaces as native editable documents at mixed canvas sizes: A3 poster, A5 programme cover, a fixed 1200x1600 shop listing mockup, 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 social, the artwork specification page with the recovered crest inline as real editable vector, and the single-root probe exports that are the only way anything past page one can actually be looked at.

A persisted, shareable place where the trust committee reviews the whole package in one view before the meeting, carrying raster proofs of the plate set, both crest states and the three colourway listings. Visited twice, because the board is populated before the corrections land and has to carry the corrected set by the time the committee sees it.

trajectory.action: Upload every client asset headlessly (initialize, PUT the bytes, finalize) and inline-preview each one before deciding anything.
trajectory.reasoning: Nothing downstream can be chosen without looking. The three crest-bearing images look interchangeable in a file list and are not, and the three garment shots only reveal their light difference side by side.
trajectory.produces: Presigned URLs for all nine client assets plus a first visual read of each.

trajectory.action: Triage the three crest-bearing sources and commit to a role for each: the 1974 scan is the geometry source; the enamel badge photo is a colour reference only and is never traced; the oxblood supporters' tee is not a geometry source but is the only surviving record of the aged screened texture and is therefore the source of exactly one pass.
trajectory.reasoning: This is the engagement's first fork and it is a three-way call, not a two-way one. Tracing the enamel badge yields the raised metal lip as a second outline around every colour cell; tracing the tee yields fabric weave. Discarding the tee entirely loses the one thing the members explicitly asked to keep. All three wrong answers return plausible-looking results.
trajectory.produces: A written source decision: geometry from the scan, colour read by eye from the badge, texture from the tee, garment shape from the tees.

trajectory.action: Select the crest at ink level off the yellowed scan by naming the graphic's own visual properties rather than the substrate it sits on, request the bounding box, then invert the selection and crop to the returned bounds.
trajectory.reasoning: Naming the programme cover or the crest on the page pulls the selection to the paper and returns a rectangle of yellowed card. Naming the oxblood heron line drawing and the sand weir bars pulls it to the ink. Inversion before vectorizing is what makes the mark positive instead of a black box, and both polarities report success.
trajectory.produces: A clean, correctly polarised binary plate of the full crest, cropped to the artwork.

trajectory.action: Vectorize the full-crest plate, pull the SVG down locally, inject a viewBox and delete the opaque full-canvas path, and keep the result as the master.
trajectory.reasoning: The vectorizer emits no viewBox and writes an opaque background rectangle as its first path. On the master, sitting on the white specification page, the agent can see the need and fix it. Whether that fix generalises to everything else it is about to trace is not yet a question anyone has been forced to ask.
trajectory.produces: master_crest_full.svg, scalable and transparent.

trajectory.action: Build one knockout plate per printed element by selecting each element by what it IS (the heron figure, the weir bars, the name scroll, the date ring lettering), inverting, and flattening everything else to white on the original scan.
trajectory.reasoning: Separation cannot be done by hue: the selection tool refuses colour and region framings outright. The plates must be cut by naming objects, and the scroll and the date ring have to be taken separately or the ring's counters ride along with the scroll.
trajectory.produces: Four element-isolated raster plates at scan resolution.

trajectory.action: Vectorize each of the four plates, and build the under-white by flattening the union of the plate paths into a single silhouette.
trajectory.reasoning: The printer wants each pass as its own file, and the under-white is a derived plate rather than a fifth drawing. The union is the obvious way to derive it and it is built from exactly the files that came back from the tracer.
trajectory.produces: Four spot-plate SVGs plus underbase_silhouette.svg.

trajectory.action: Build the composite proof the printer asked for: a single-root probe document on the club's oxblood ground with the under-white laid beneath the four plates stacked in pass order and the master crest alongside for comparison. Run the readiness check, export, then find the document, resolve its rendition and look at the rendered page.
trajectory.reasoning: A separation is only true as a composite, and this is the first moment the plates exist in the same space as each other and on the club's own ground colour rather than on a white page. A single root is used deliberately because only page one of a rendition can be previewed, so anything that must be judged by eye has to be made page one.
trajectory.produces: Two findings that did not exist before the stack was assembled: the under-white silhouette renders as a solid full-canvas block that occludes every plate above it, and once that block is set aside the composite does not match the master, with two of the four weir bars absent from the bar plate.

trajectory.action: Return to the plate and underbase stage: strip the surviving opaque full-canvas path out of every plate SVG, inject the missing viewBoxes, then re-flatten the union so the silhouette is the union of the artwork rather than the union of four canvases.
trajectory.reasoning: The block is not a plate defect and it is not visible on any individual plate or on a white page; it is what the union of four opaque canvas rectangles resolves to. It was created by the derivation at step 6 and it cannot be papered over in a layout, because the under-white is the first ink down.
trajectory.produces: Corrected plate SVGs, transparent and scalable, and a genuine underbase silhouette that traces the mark.

trajectory.action: Return to the selection stage and re-cut the incomplete plate: take the weir bars as individual per-bar selections and composite them rather than naming the bar group once, then re-run the fill, crop and vectorize for that plate only.
trajectory.reasoning: Selection on a compound element comes back plausible and incomplete, with success reported and nothing in the response indicating what was dropped. The correction is a different selection strategy, not a retry of the same one, and it has to happen on the raster before anything is traced again.
trajectory.produces: A complete weir-bar plate raster and its corrected SVG.

trajectory.action: Re-export the composite proof probe and confirm the stack now reproduces the master with nothing missing and no block, then keep the proof as a deliverable for the printer.
trajectory.reasoning: Forced propagation after steps 8 and 9 changed the plate set, and the printer asked for this proof by name because he has been burned by a missing piece before. It is not a new discovery; it is the confirmation the corrections landed.
trajectory.produces: A verified composite proof of the separation set, retained as a client deliverable.

trajectory.action: Assign the club's colours as local fill edits inside the SVG text: the oxblood and the sand chosen by eye off the enamel badge photograph and applied to the master and to the plates, then recombine the heron and bar paths in oxblood with the scroll and ring paths in sand into a two-ink lockup.
trajectory.reasoning: Nothing about vectorizing a yellowed two-ink print puts the club's colours into the artwork; the trace preserves the aged hues. There is no eyedropper anywhere in the toolset and no route to a named hue through the adjustment tools, so the colour is a judgement made against a bevelled, specular, window-lit photograph and it has to be owned and reported as chosen rather than claimed as sampled.
trajectory.produces: Colour-assigned master and plate SVGs plus the two-ink lockup, with both chosen hex values stated as the agent's own reading.

trajectory.action: Build the simplified single-colour small-use mark by subtraction and solidification on the plate rasters: erase the date ring with a masked fill, fill the heron solid so its interior feather and leg detail are deliberately surrendered, set the weir bars solid, drop the scroll's inner rule, then crop to bounds and vectorize. Produce it also as a raster at the card's 24mm reproduction scale, built down from the scan rather than up from anything small.
trajectory.reasoning: The printer briefed 24mm on the sleeve badge and smaller on the neck label at the outset, so this is commissioned work, not a discovery. Reaching a minimum line weight is done by removing thin elements, not by fattening them; the craft judgement being made is how much detail can be surrendered before the heron stops being the heron, and it is reported as worked to by eye.
trajectory.produces: crest_mark_simplified.svg and crest_mark_simplified.png at card scale, plus a written note on what was surrendered and why.

trajectory.action: Produce the aged-texture pass off the supporters' tee photograph: mask the printed lettering and heron out, screen only the surrounding field to monochrome dots at a chosen radius, keep the result as a one-bit raster, and compute and state the largest finished print size at which the pass still holds.
trajectory.reasoning: The texture is a photographic record of a real screened print on fabric, so it comes from the garment shot and nowhere else. Vectorizing a halftone would explode into thousands of near-identical paths and is the wrong artefact to hand a screen printer. The radius is a taste call, but the honest question is how big it can go, and since nothing may be interpolated up, that number is a declared limitation rather than an assumption.
trajectory.produces: texture_pass.png at native scale, lettering crisp, field screened, with its stated maximum reproduction size.

trajectory.action: Run the recommender once for the display and nameset role and once for the text role, pull the full style inventory to learn the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and mint one embed kit for the whole system, then re-typeset the club wordmark in the chosen display face.
trajectory.reasoning: The tool refuses to pair, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction. Family weights are non-standard, so the reflexive 400 can silently ship a Light face, and the client's only wordmark file is a 320-pixel PNG that cannot be enlarged, so the wordmark has to be set rather than scaled.
trajectory.produces: A two-role type system with real numeric weights, one embeddable kit, and a re-typeset wordmark.

trajectory.action: Export a single-root probe of the artwork specification sheet on the club's oxblood ground: the crest system, the plate proofs, a specimen row showing the crest at chest, sleeve and neck-label sizes, and a type specimen of both roles. Preview the rendition and parse the returned markup for the faces that actually resolved.
trajectory.reasoning: Everything about the type looks correct in the CSS. The only evidence of what a face actually became is what the importer reports back, and the specimen row is the first time the small-use mark is seen at real size on a real canvas rather than assumed to work.
trajectory.produces: The finding that the display cut did not take: the returned markup reports a plain roman face where the nameset was specified, because an optical display cut is a family of its own and is not reachable by asking its roman family for a heavier weight.

trajectory.action: Return to the type stage: resolve the display cut through the name-laundering tool to get its own canonical form, rebuild the whole kit in one call because the kit is all-or-nothing and one bad name discards the rest, then rewrite the family and the numeric weight on the text elements themselves and re-probe until the markup reports the intended faces.
trajectory.reasoning: The defect was created at the type stage and is invisible everywhere except in what comes back from the importer. No amount of CSS care at the layout stage fixes a family that was never in the kit, and shipping it means the club's name is set in the wrong face across every canvas.
trajectory.produces: A corrected kit and stylesheet, with the intended faces confirmed present in the returned markup.

trajectory.action: Straighten all three garment photographs and bring each one to a defensible result on its own terms: auto-tone, then correct the tungsten and the overcast casts toward the house look, then crop each subject-aware to the shop listing ratio, reading the returned tradeoffs to confirm nothing was interpolated up.
trajectory.reasoning: Two volunteers, three days, tungsten, LED and overcast. Each image is judged and corrected as it comes, which is what any sane process does at this stage, and the resize tool will silently interpolate up to twice source size while mentioning it only in a tradeoffs array that is easy to ignore.
trajectory.produces: Three graded garment masters and three listing-ratio crops, no upscaling.

trajectory.action: Knock each garment out to transparent RGBA and crop to the subject bounds, preserving alpha through the crop.
trajectory.reasoning: A transparent cutout is the general-purpose answer and it is what you reach for when one set of images has to serve both the shop page and the printed card. Nothing yet contradicts it.
trajectory.produces: Three transparent garment cutouts at listing ratio.

trajectory.action: Create a persistent board for the trust committee and place the review set on it as rasters: the four plate proofs, the texture pass, the full crest plate, the simplified mark and the three colourway listings, submitted as presigned URLs in one call, with the failed-items list checked and anything that failed re-sent.
trajectory.reasoning: The club asked for one place the committee can look at everything before the meeting. The board will not take vector at all, so the reviewable artefact is a raster proof and the production file is not, and that is a distinction the agent has to draw rather than discover by shipping an empty board.
trajectory.produces: A live board URL carrying ten placed items, nothing failed.

trajectory.action: Search stock with a short query, license one floodlit terrace photograph at camera scale, download it inside the licence window, and bring it down to the A3 poster ground and the 9:16 story canvas.
trajectory.reasoning: The club owns no crowd photography and no photograph may be invented. Licensed stock is the only clean source, long queries return nothing, the orientation filter is broken, and the frame must be downscaled only.
trajectory.produces: One licensed terrace frame, cropped to the poster ratio and to 9:16, never enlarged.

trajectory.action: Author the full campaign as one document at mixed canvas sizes: A3 poster, A5 Boxing Day programme cover, the shop listing mockup on a fixed 1200x1600 canvas, 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 social, plus the corrected specification page. Every photograph base64-inlined, the crest present as inline vector, the campaign lockups using the low-path simplified mark. Upload the HTML and export it by reference because the payload is far past the inline limit.
trajectory.reasoning: Photographs referenced by URL come through as empty grey boxes at full success, including from the connector's own asset hosts, so inlining is a requirement rather than an optimisation. The shop page is authored as a fixed-canvas mockup rather than anything responsive, because responsive-shaped input routes to a gate that stops the run. The full crest lands as dozens of ungrouped paths, so the mark that carries the campaign lockups is the low-path one the volunteers can actually move.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document carrying seven roots at their true canvas sizes, plus the source HTML.

trajectory.action: Verify properly rather than by success code: export a single-root probe of the shop listing page with all three colourways adjacent on the club's ground, preview it, and parse the campaign's returned markup for faces, tables and image fills.
trajectory.reasoning: Only page one of a rendition previews, so the page that has to be judged by eye is made its own probe. This is also the first time the three garments have ever been adjacent, at final crop, on a coloured ground, and the first time the licensed frame has been seen inside the actual lockups.
trajectory.produces: Three findings: the transparent cutouts carry a pale fringe and each collar opening is still filled with garage floor; the sand colourway reads warmer than the other two in company even though each was defensible alone; and the terrace frame's pylon, which is why it was chosen, falls outside the 9:16 crop while at A3 the crowd sits behind the lockup with nothing to read.

trajectory.action: Return to stock and license a differently composed, portrait-friendlier terrace frame, then bring it down to both canvases and re-place it.
trajectory.reasoning: The crop tool only takes pixels away, so a wider frame cannot be made taller, and outpainting invented supporters into a licensed photograph of real people is refused on editorial grounds at a club whose buyers are the people in the stand. The only honest route is a different frame, and that means going back to the surface that supplied it.
trajectory.produces: A second licensed terrace frame that survives both the poster ratio and the story crop, downscaled only.

trajectory.action: Return to the grade: pull the sand colourway's white point and warmth back until it sits with the other two, judged against the pair rather than against itself.
trajectory.reasoning: Nothing was wrong with the sand image alone, which is exactly why it survived step 17. What it fails is company, at final size, against a ground colour, and that judgement could not be made before those three conditions existed together. The grade has to be corrected before the knockout, because the knockout composites whatever the grade produced.
trajectory.produces: A re-graded sand master that holds with the navy and the oxblood.

trajectory.action: Return to the knockout and repair it in two moves: re-run the background removal compositing straight onto the shop ground colour, which removes the pale fringe, then on that result select the visible garage floor showing through the collar by naming it positively as the material it is, fill that mask with the ground colour, and re-crop. Keep the transparent set unchanged as a separate artefact.
trajectory.reasoning: The knockout cannot punch an enclosed interior, and compositing onto a ground colour does not change what the subject mask contains, so it fixes the fringe and nothing about the hole; the hole needs a second, positive selection because the tool rejects framings like the background or the hole. The transparent set is kept because on white card stock a filled collar is invisible, which is only now obvious as a fact about destinations rather than a preference.
trajectory.produces: A ground-matched cutout set for the shop listing and a retained transparent set, with the reason each exists written down.

trajectory.action: Re-inline the corrected garments and the second terrace frame, re-run the readiness check, re-export the campaign, and re-probe both the shop listing page and the story canvas.
trajectory.reasoning: Forced propagation after steps 23, 24 and 25 changed the images the document carries. Every re-export needs the readiness pass again, and the campaign is only finished when the listing page holds three garments that read as one line.
trajectory.produces: The corrected campaign document plus its source HTML.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's A6 card PDF to a native document, export its interchange format, unzip it and reconstruct each frame's true story text from the content runs, compute every replacement offset from that reconstructed string, validate, build the merge template with two image columns bound (the garment swatch varying per row and the crest identical on every row), then re-export the interchange file and grep it to confirm every placeholder landed and that both graphic frames carry merge markers.
trajectory.reasoning: The mapping tool's reported text content silently drops runs while keeping their line breaks, so offsets taken from it are wrong by the length of the omission, the validator still says valid, and the template still reports success while shipping fields short. The card's small kit office email line is exactly the kind of run that goes missing. The crest is static across the run but there is only one verified way to bind an image at all, so it rides the same mechanism with the same filename on every row.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template carrying placeholders for name, number, size, colourway and season plus two verified bound image frames.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster without stalling: normalise the six size tokens to one canonical set, and for the duplicated squad number, the blank size and the two spellings of one player's own surname, record each as an open query with the provisional value used, stated in writing, then merge all eighteen records to a native document and render 300 dpi proofs.
trajectory.reasoning: Merging a dirty roster produces eighteen confidently wrong cards, but the club has said explicitly not to wait on them, and a run that blocks on an answer that never comes has failed a job it was otherwise doing correctly. The judgement being graded is the flagging and the stated assumption, not a guess dressed as a decision.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned 18-row roster with an open-query list, a merged document, and 300 dpi proof cards.

trajectory.action: Inspect the proofs at print size and read what the card's own frames do to the placed images.
trajectory.reasoning: The crest holds at the card's 24mm box, which is what building a real small-use mark at step 12 bought. The swatch does not: the printer's swatch box is wider than it is tall and the garment crops were cut portrait for the shop listing, so each shirt is being fitted into a landscape frame and reads as a cropped band with the sleeves gone.
trajectory.produces: The finding that the card needs its own crop of the garments, and that the frame's proportions are a fact about the client's file rather than a preference.

trajectory.action: Return to the cutout stage and cut a second, card-specific garment set from the graded masters to the swatch frame's proportions, transparent alpha retained for white stock, checking the tradeoffs to confirm nothing was interpolated up.
trajectory.reasoning: A crop is made for a frame, and this frame was not known until the client's own file was opened and its output looked at. Re-scaling the listing crop would only letterbox the same wrong shape, and the card set has to come down from the graded master, not up from a small file.
trajectory.produces: Three card-scale garment cutouts at the swatch frame's proportions.

trajectory.action: Re-point the CSV's image column at the card-specific cutouts, re-merge all eighteen records, and deliver both branches: one press file at one card per page, and eighteen separate single-page files named to the roster, plus 300 dpi proofs.
trajectory.reasoning: Forced propagation after step 30 changed the bound images, and re-merging is the only way the correction reaches all eighteen cards. Per-record files must come from the separate-files branch, because the multi-record raster branch returns its outputs in an order its own labels contradict.
trajectory.produces: An 18-page press PDF, 18 per-player named single-page PDFs, and 300 dpi proofs.

trajectory.action: Replace the board's superseded items with the corrected raster set so the committee reviews what will actually be printed, checking the failed-items list again.
trajectory.reasoning: Forced propagation: the board was populated at step 19 with plates and listings that have since been corrected twice, and a committee voting on superseded artwork is worse than no board at all.
trajectory.produces: The committee board carrying the final review set.

trajectory.action: Finish the artwork and print handover sheet and deliver it twice: as a page inside the editable campaign document for the volunteers, and as the standalone source HTML file for the printer, who opens it in a browser. It states which mark at which size and why, the pass order, which garments take the under-white and which must not, the screened texture radius as applied and its maximum reproduction size, the grade and crop parameters as applied, the two chosen club hex values stated as a by-eye reading of the badge, the type system with its real numeric weights, foundries and designers, the open roster queries with the provisional values used, and a warning that the full crest arrives in the editable document as many ungrouped paths.
trajectory.reasoning: The printer has no design software and cannot be handed an Express document, and nothing can be exported out of one anyway, so the sheet has to exist in a form he can open. The volunteers have to be able to do next season without the freelancer, which means being told the things that will otherwise bite them.
trajectory.produces: The handover sheet as an editable page and as a standalone HTML file, plus the full parameter report.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: Laid on the club's oxblood with the four plates stacked above it, the derived under-white does not read as a silhouette of the crest at all; it renders as a solid full-canvas block that hides every plate above it. Nothing about any individual plate showed this, and on a white page the composite would have looked correct.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The union that produced the underbase has to be rebuilt: the opaque full-canvas path that rides along on every trace must be stripped from all four plate files and the missing viewBoxes injected, so that flattening them yields the union of the artwork rather than the union of four canvases. The layout cannot compensate, because the under-white is the first ink laid down.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The printer burns an under-white screen that is a solid rectangle. Every navy and oxblood garment goes through the press with a white block printed across the chest and the crest laid on top of it, and the sleeve badge and neck label print as white patches with the mark inside. On screen at poster size on a light ground it all looks perfect.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: With the block set aside, the composite of the four plates does not reproduce the master: two of the four weir bars are missing. The bar plate was cut in one selection, that selection returned success, the mask looked plausible, and no tool response anywhere indicated that anything had been dropped.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The bar plate has to be re-cut with a different strategy, not retried with the same one: each bar selected individually and the masks composited, then re-filled, re-cropped and re-traced. This is a raster-stage correction and it has to happen before anything is vectorized again.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The chest print goes to press with half the weir under the heron, which is the element that makes the crest Thornbeck's rather than any club with a bird on it. The error is carried identically into the sleeve badge, the neck label, the poster, the programme cover and all eighteen kit-order cards, because every one of them is fed from the same plate set.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The markup that comes back from the importer reports a plain roman face where the nameset and display role was specified. The stylesheet was correct, the kit built without error, and the page rendered without complaint; the only place the substitution is visible is in what the importer says it resolved.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The display cut has to be reached as the separate family it actually is, resolved through the name-laundering tool and rebuilt into the kit in a single call, then written onto the text elements with its own family and its own numeric weight. Asking a roman family for a heavier weight will never produce it.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The club's name and the shirt nameset are set in the wrong face on the poster, the programme cover, the shop page and the whole social set, consistently and confidently, and the volunteers inherit a document whose type does not match the handover sheet that credits a foundry and a designer who were never used.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: In the finished lockups, the licensed terrace frame does not do the job it was licensed for. The floodlight pylon that made the frame worth choosing falls outside the 9:16 story crop, and at A3 the crowd sits behind the crest lockup with nothing left to read. Neither was knowable from the frame on its own or from its dimensions.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: A differently composed frame has to be licensed. The crop tool only removes pixels, so a wide frame cannot be made tall, and outpainting invented supporters into a licensed photograph of real people is refused here on editorial grounds at a club whose buyers are the people in that stand. The return is to the stock surface, not to the layout.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The story post ships with the pylon cut off and a band of empty terrace, and the poster ships with an expensive photograph doing no work behind the type, which at 58 pounds to the club's own members reads as filler rather than as the ground.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: Seen adjacent, at final crop, on the club's ground colour, the sand colourway reads warmer than the navy and the oxblood. Each of the three was corrected and each was defensible on its own screen; the failure only exists in company and only at the size and on the ground where the shop page puts them.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The sand master's white point and warmth have to be pulled back until it sits with the pair rather than with itself, and this has to happen before the knockout is redone, because the knockout composites whatever the grade produced.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The shop page ships three shirts that plainly came from three different shops, which is the exact complaint the client raised in the brief and paid to have fixed.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: Against the shop's dark ground the transparent cutouts show a pale fringe around every edge, and each collar opening is still filled with a patch of garage floor. On the white page where the cutouts were made and checked, both are invisible.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: The knockout needs two moves rather than one: composite the subject straight onto the shop ground colour, which removes the fringe, and then, because that does nothing to what the subject mask contains and the tool cannot punch an enclosed interior, select the visible floor inside the collar positively by the material it is and fill it with the ground colour before re-cropping. The transparent set is retained rather than replaced, because the destination it was wrong for is not the only destination.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: The shop listing ships three shirts with grey halos and a rectangle of garage floor showing through each collar, on the page the whole launch links to.

revisit_loops.what_is_learned: The 300 dpi proof shows the garment swatch fitted into the printer's swatch box as a cropped band with the sleeves gone. The box on his card is wider than it is tall; the cutouts were cut portrait for the shop listing. The frame's proportions are a fact about a client file that was not opened until step 27.
revisit_loops.what_must_change: A second, card-specific garment set has to be cut from the graded masters to the swatch frame's proportions, keeping the transparent alpha that white card stock wants, and it must come down from the master rather than be rescaled from the listing crop, which would only letterbox the same wrong shape.
revisit_loops.what_breaks_if_skipped: Eighteen kit-order cards go to the printer showing a horizontal slice of a shirt, so the one thing the card exists to communicate, which colourway the player chose, is the thing it fails to show.

deliverables.name: Recovered crest vector system
deliverables.spec: Two marks, not a mark and its recolours: the full crest recovered from the 1974 scan geometry with the club's colours applied as chosen by eye from the enamel badge, and a genuinely simplified single-colour small-use mark for 24mm and below built by subtraction and solid fill. Every file transparent, every file carrying a viewBox, no full-canvas path anywhere, and the small-use mark demonstrably not a scaled reduction of the full one. Both hex values stated as the agent's own reading rather than claimed as measured.

deliverables.name: Screen-print separation set with composite proof
deliverables.spec: One file per pass as the printer asked: heron, weir bars, name scroll, date ring, plus a derived under-white silhouette flagged for the navy and oxblood garments only and explicitly excluded from the sand, plus the aged-texture pass as a one-bit screened raster taken off the supporters' tee with the lettering held crisp and its maximum reproduction size stated. Includes the composite proof the printer asked for, showing every pass stacked back together in pass order against the recovered master, and the two-ink lockup as a stated recombination of these plates. Pass order stated.

deliverables.name: Shop and card garment sets
deliverables.spec: Three garment photographs, straightened, corrected across two volunteers and three lighting conditions until they hold together at final crop on the club's ground, subject-aware cropped with no interpolation above source, and delivered as two sets for two destinations: knocked out onto the shop ground colour at the listing proportions, and knocked out with transparent alpha at the printer's swatch-box proportions. The reason each set exists is stated.

deliverables.name: Squad kit-order run
deliverables.spec: Eighteen records from the reconciled roster, one card per page: a single 18-page press PDF in roster order, eighteen separate single-page PDFs named to each player for the February reorders, and 300 dpi proofs for the kit office. Each card carries that player's name, squad number, size, the garment swatch bound per row to the agent's own card-scale cutouts, and the simplified crest bound identically on every row. Open roster queries listed with the provisional value used on the cards.

deliverables.name: 125th-season launch campaign
deliverables.spec: One native editable document at mixed canvas sizes: A3 poster, A5 Boxing Day programme cover against Aldercar Town, a shop listing page mockup on a fixed 1200x1600 canvas rather than a responsive layout, and a social set at 1080x1080, 1080x1350 and 1080x1920. One type system in the actually-resolved faces, one crest system, every photograph inlined and rendering, the campaign lockups carrying the low-path simplified mark so a volunteer can move it, and the full crest supplied alongside as a standalone vector file.

deliverables.name: Artwork and print handover sheet
deliverables.spec: Delivered twice by design: as an editable page inside the campaign document for the club's volunteers, and as a standalone HTML file the screen printer opens in a browser with no design software. Covers which mark at which size, minimum reproduction size, pass order, which garments take the under-white and which must not, the screened texture radius as applied and the largest size it prints at, the grade and crop parameters as applied, the two club hex values and how they were arrived at, the type system with its real numeric weights and credited foundries, the open roster queries, and the warning that the full crest arrives in the editable document as many ungrouped paths.

deliverables.name: Committee review board
deliverables.spec: A persisted, shareable place the trust committee reviews the whole package in one view before it votes at the next meeting. Carries raster proofs only, because the surface will not accept vector at all: the four plate proofs, the texture pass, the full crest, the simplified mark and the three colourway listings. Item count verifiable, nothing left in the failed list, and repopulated after the corrections so the committee is not looking at superseded artwork. The vector production files ship to the printer separately and are not board items.

decision_gates: Source triage is three-way, not two-way. One image holds the crest's geometry, one holds its colour and must never be traced because its raised metal lip becomes a second outline around every colour cell, and the third is a garment photograph that is not a geometry source but is the only surviving record of one required pass. Running the same recovery on all three returns three plausible results; discarding the third loses the thing the members asked to keep.

Selection wording is the whole gate and it fails silently: naming the substrate pulls the mask to the yellowed paper and returns a rectangle, and naming the graphic's own colour, medium and form pulls it to the ink. Both succeed.
Mask polarity before vectorizing: tracing the raw mask yields a black box with the crest knocked out of it, and one inversion is the entire difference. Both outputs report success.

Separation cannot be done by colour. The selection tool rejects hue and region framings outright, so the passes must be cut by naming what each element IS, and the scroll and the date ring must be taken separately or the ring's counters ride along with the scroll.

A separation is only true as a composite. Selection on a compound element returns success on a mask that is plausible and incomplete, and nothing in any tool response says which piece is missing, so the set has to be proved back together against the recovered master before anything is trusted or handed on.
The under-white is derived, not drawn, and it is not wanted on every garment: the printer's note puts it on two of the three and forbids it on the third. Laying it everywhere is the reflexive answer.

Traced output arrives unfit for placement, and its defects are invisible on a white page and fatal on the club's own ground colour, including when several traced files are combined into a derived one.

Colour is a judgement, not a measurement. The club's two inks have to be decided from a bevelled, specular, window-lit photograph and then deliberately applied to artwork traced off a yellowed print; there is no eyedropper, no hex readout, and no route to a named hue through the adjustment tools, so the values must be stated as chosen rather than claimed as sampled.

Minimum reproduction size is a redraw problem, not a scaling problem, and the redraw is subtraction: erasing the ring, surrendering the heron's interior detail to a solid, and setting the bars solid. The gradeable judgement is how much can go before the heron stops being the heron.

The screened texture must stay raster; tracing a halftone produces thousands of near-identical paths and is the wrong artefact to hand a screen printer. The harder call is not the radius but the largest size the pass can be printed at, which has to be computed from what actually exists and declared, because nothing may be interpolated up.

No upscaling anywhere: the 320-pixel wordmark must be re-set in the chosen face rather than enlarged, and the resize tool will interpolate up to twice source size while reporting it only in a tradeoffs array that is easy to ignore.

Type is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair; family weights are non-standard so the reflexive 400 can ship a Light face; and a display cut is a family of its own that cannot be reached by asking its roman family for more weight. The only evidence a face took is what the importer reports back, never what was written in the stylesheet.

Grading is judged where the work finally sits. An image that is defensible on its own screen can be wrong in company, at final crop, on a coloured ground, and the correction has to go back to the master rather than be patched in the layout.

A knockout that is right for one destination is not automatically right for another, and the tool's knockout has a limit that only shows on a dark ground. Compositing onto a ground colour and punching an interior are two different problems with two different answers, and the second one needs the interior named positively as the material it is.

A crop is made for a frame, and the frame's proportions are a fact about the client's file rather than a preference. One crop cannot serve two frames of different shape, and the second crop has to come down from the master.

Photographs referenced by URL render as empty boxes at full success, including from the connector's own asset hosts, so every image must be inlined; the finished payload is far past the inline limit, so the document must reach the importer by reference from an allowed host; and a page shaped like a responsive layout rather than a fixed canvas routes to a gate that stops the run.

Only the first page of a rendition can be previewed, so anything that must be judged by eye has to be deliberately put in front of the eye as its own single-root export. Success codes are not fidelity, and every silent drop returns success.

Merge-template offset integrity: the mapping tool's reported text drops runs while keeping their line breaks, so offsets computed from it are wrong, the validator still passes them, the template still reports success, and fields silently vanish from all eighteen cards. Offsets must come from the reconstructed story text, and the rebuilt template must be re-opened and checked rather than believed.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a one-shot image model and it will draw a heron. That is the failure. The club's crest has been on their shirts since 1901 and the entire commission is the recovery of that specific geometry, misregistration and all, from a yellowed 1974 print; a regenerated crest is a different club's crest and the members will say so out loud. Identity fails immediately, and it fails again on the photographs: the three garment shots are the club's actual stock on their actual garage floor, and the client is paying to have those made consistent, not replaced with invented shirts. Spec fails next: nothing regenerated is separated into named passes with an under-white restricted to two of three garments and a composite proof that reconciles back to the master, nothing regenerated is eighteen single-page press files bound to a real roster with each player's own name, number, size and colourway, nothing regenerated respects a 24mm minimum reproduction size or a 0.6mm minimum line weight, and nothing regenerated tells the printer the largest size his texture screen holds at. Editability fails last and hardest: the club is supporter-owned and staffed by volunteers, and the whole handover premise is that they keep working on these files in-house next season, which means live vector paths, live text in a licensed face, a live merge template, and a handover sheet the printer can open on a machine with no design software. A picture of a poster satisfies none of it.

human_difficulty: A skilled freelancer would quote this at several days and still lose an evening to it. The crest exists twice and neither copy is authoritative: the 1974 print holds the geometry but has drifted out of register and yellowed, the enamel badge holds the colour but is bevelled, tilted and full of speculars, and reconciling one against the other is a judgement nobody can check against an original because no original survives. A third image looks like a third copy of the crest and is not, but it is also not a decoy, because it is the only record of a texture the members would notice missing, so the triage is a three-way call in which two of the plausible answers are wrong in opposite directions. Separations then carry the trap every screen printer has been burned by: four plates that each look right individually and do not add up, which is exactly why he asked for a composite proof, and why a freelancer who ships without one eventually ships wrong shirts. The same mark has to work at 380mm on a chest and 24mm on a sleeve, which means drawing a second mark rather than scaling the first, and knowing how much detail to surrender before the heron stops being the heron is the part clients notice and cannot articulate. An under-white on the wrong garment ruins the sand shirts and the printer will not catch it. The three garment photographs come from two volunteers on three days, and consistency across a set is a different skill from making one image look good; worse, the failure is not visible on the light table, only in company at final crop on a coloured ground, which is late. Cutouts made for a white page have two separate defects that a dark page reveals at once, and they need two different repairs. A crop cut for a shop listing does not fit a frame in the client's own press file that nobody had opened yet. The roster is dirty in ways that require asking rather than deciding, on a deadline that forbids waiting, so the craft is in flagging well. And the whole thing has to hold as one identity across a screen-printed garment, a variable-data print run, a poster, a programme cover and a phone screen, at a price band where restraint is the product. Nearly every failure mode here is invisible on the freelancer's own screen and appears only on the printer's press, on the club's dark shop page, or in what a file quietly reports back rather than what it displays, which is exactly why real jobs like this loop back three and four times before they ship.
